title: Greece Approves 10% Crypto Gains Tax, 15% Levy on Staking and DeFi Income
summary: Greece’s parliament has approved a sweeping cryptocurrency tax framework that imposes a 10% tax on capital gains and a separate 15% tax on income from staking, lending, and decentralized finance (DeFi), marking the country’s first comprehensive approach to taxing digital assets. Greece Adopts Crypto...
content:
Greece’s parliament has approved a sweeping cryptocurrency tax framework that imposes a 10% tax on capital gains and a separate 15% tax on income from staking, lending, and decentralized finance (DeFi), marking the country’s first comprehensive approach to taxing digital assets.

Key Takeaways

  • Greece approved a 10% tax on annual cryptocurrency capital gains exceeding €500, effective Jan. 1, 2027, with losses eligible for a five-year carryforward.
  • Staking, crypto lending, and DeFi earnings will face a separate 15% income tax, while cryptocurrency inheritances and gifts will receive clarified tax treatment.
  • Investors will have a 12-month window to voluntarily disclose previously unreported crypto gains without penalties or interest, while regulators work to clarify the treatment of crypto-to-crypto swaps.

Greece Adopts Crypto Tax Law

The legislation, approved Thursday, Nov. 5, will take effect on Jan. 1, 2027, and establishes new reporting requirements, exemptions, and provisions allowing investors to declare previously unreported cryptocurrency profits without penalties.

Under the new rules, individuals will pay a 10% tax on annual net cryptocurrency gains exceeding €500 (approximately $560). Gains below that threshold are exempt, but once the limit is exceeded, the entire taxable gain becomes subject to the levy rather than only the portion above €500.

The tax applies to profits from selling cryptocurrencies for traditional currency, as well as using digital assets to purchase goods and services. Contributing cryptocurrencies to a company’s capital also constitutes a taxable transfer under Article 48 of the legislation.

Investors who incur annual net cryptocurrency losses exceeding €500 can carry those losses forward for five years, using them to offset future cryptocurrency capital gains.

The legislation also establishes a separate tax treatment for cryptocurrency income generated through staking, lending, and DeFi activities. Article 47 classifies returns from crypto lending, liquidity provision, yield farming, and participation in blockchain transaction validation as interest income, making them subject to Greece’s 15% tax rate.

When such income is paid in cryptocurrency rather than cash, its taxable value is determined using the asset’s euro-denominated price at the time of the transaction.

Another significant provision gives cryptocurrency investors a 12-month opportunity to voluntarily disclose gains and qualifying crypto income earned before the new rules take effect. Taxpayers who participate can avoid late-filing penalties and interest, provided they pay the taxes owed within 60 days of filing their declarations.

The legislation also clarifies the treatment of cryptocurrency holdings received through inheritance, gifts, and parental transfers, establishing valuation rules based on prices from recognized trading platforms. Cryptocurrency sales are additionally exempted from Greece’s digital transaction tax.

However, uncertainty remains over whether exchanging one cryptocurrency for another will trigger capital gains taxes. While Greece’s Finance Ministry has indicated that crypto-to-crypto swaps will not be taxable, the Greek parliament’s Scientific Service warned that the legislation’s wording could potentially encompass such transactions.

Further regulatory guidance is expected to clarify how the rules will operate.

“Further implementation directives will be published in the coming weeks, which will also define transparency and audit rules,” a senior Finance Ministry official told Reuters.

The official said the government could not reliably estimate how much revenue the new taxes would generate because most Greek cryptocurrency investors use foreign trading platforms, making the domestic market difficult to measure.

The changes come as European countries continue developing different approaches to cryptocurrency taxation. Unlike the European Union’s increasingly unified framework for regulating digital assets, member states retain responsibility for establishing their own tax policies.

According to Reuters, cryptocurrency tax rates across European countries range from approximately 8% to 30%, with most jurisdictions focusing primarily on capital gains.

title: CFTC Tells Prediction Markets to Drop State Geoblocks Within 30 Days
summary: The Commodity Futures Trading Commission says federally regulated prediction markets generally cannot block traders based on which U.S. state they are in, and has given exchanges 30 days to lift such restrictions or explain why they can’t. The guidance came a day after a federal judge ordered Kalshi...
content:
The Commodity Futures Trading Commission says federally regulated prediction markets generally cannot block traders based on which U.S. state they are in, and has given exchanges 30 days to lift such restrictions or explain why they can’t. The guidance came a day after a federal judge ordered Kalshi to block sports contracts on the lands of California tribes that sued it.

Key Takeaways

  • The CFTC gave exchanges 30 days to end state-by-state geographic restrictions or explain why they can’t.
  • Exchanges must also make sure brokers and other intermediaries don’t impose their own geoblocks.
  • A judge ordered Kalshi on Nov. 4 to block sports contracts on the lands of California tribes that sued it.

CFTC Says Geographic Restrictions Break Federal Rules

The CFTC on Thursday, Nov. 5, issued an interpretation of its impartial access rule, which requires designated contract markets (DCMs) to give eligible traders “competitive, open, fair, and impartial access.” The agency gave exchanges 30 days to end state-level geoblocks: DCMs “must cease domestic geographic restrictions that violate the Impartial Access Requirements within 30 days,” or else explain to the CFTC’s Division of Market Oversight why compliance is not feasible.

“Derivatives markets must operate on a uniform basis at a national scale in order to achieve the purposes set out in the Commodity Exchange Act,” CFTC Chairman Michael Selig said. “Geographic access restrictions are inconsistent with those purposes and the Act’s impartial access requirements.”

The same 30-day window applies to intermediaries, such as brokers that route customers to an exchange. DCMs should ensure those firms are not impeding impartial access, or explain why they can’t. The CFTC said it “will consider the facts and circumstances of any particular case” in connection with any potential action.

Why the CFTC Opposes Geoblocking

In the six-page interpretation, the agency said federal law and its rules “generally do not permit a DCM to limit access based on the location of an otherwise eligible market participant within the United States.” It takes effect when published in the Federal Register.

The CFTC listed several harms, highlighting that a trader who opens a position in a state where access is allowed and then travels to one where it is blocked could be unable to manage the position or meet margin calls. Blocking states can also fragment liquidity and lead to wider spreads, according to the agency.

A contract on “whether a home team advances to its playoffs” could lose liquidity if that team’s region were excluded, the agency added, while stating that in election markets “the most informed trading may be sourced on a state or local basis.” The interpretation does not mention court orders, state regulators, or tribes.

Guidance Collides With Court Orders Against Kalshi

The guidance lands as exchanges face court-ordered geoblocks. On Nov. 4, U.S. District Judge Jacqueline Scott Corley granted a preliminary injunction in a suit brought by California tribes including Blue Lake Rancheria. The order bars Kalshi from offering “any sports contracts” on the tribes’ Indian lands. The tribes must send Kalshi maps of those lands by Nov. 13, and Kalshi must report on its compliance within 21 days.

In Michigan, Kalshi is already under a state-court injunction that requires it to geofence Michigan users, with violations carrying a $500,000 daily fine. Several federal courts have also rejected Kalshi’s argument that blocking a state would breach the impartial access rule, according to NEXTPredict, including the Ninth Circuit in Kalshi’s Nevada case, which called it a “false, all-or-nothing proposition.”

States are also stepping up their own cases. Arkansas Attorney General Tim Griffin sued Kalshi on Nov. 4 under the state’s Deceptive Trade Practices Act, while the CFTC has sued Utah to stop it from enforcing its gambling laws against federally regulated prediction markets.

The announcement does allow exchanges to submit an explanation of why compliance is not feasible within the 30 days, but it does not say how the agency would treat one, including from an exchange under a court-ordered geoblock.

title: Terawulf and IREN Bet Big on AI as Bitcoin Mining Revenue Shrinks
summary: Despite top-line growth, Terawulf’s operating loss widened to $88.2 million in Q3 while IREN saw bitcoin mining revenue fall 88% year-over-year. Operating Losses Widen Amid Rising Costs For the third quarter of 2026, U.S. digital infrastructure provider Terawulf generated $76.2 million in total reve...
content:
Despite top-line growth, Terawulf’s operating loss widened to $88.2 million in Q3 while IREN saw bitcoin mining revenue fall 88% year-over-year.

Key Takeaways

  • Terawulf’s Q3 2026 HPC lease revenue reached $63 million, driving total revenue to $76.2 million.
  • Bitcoin miners like Terawulf and IREN are shifting to AI cloud services as mining revenues plunge.
  • Terawulf will expand its Muskie campus to 1 GW and begin delivering Anthropic data centers by late 2027.

Operating Losses Widen Amid Rising Costs

For the third quarter of 2026, U.S. digital infrastructure provider Terawulf generated $76.2 million in total revenue, a significant year-over-year (YoY) increase driven primarily by its high-performance computing (HPC) data center leasing segment. HPC revenue surged to $63 million, accounting for roughly 83% of the top line.

Conversely, bitcoin mining and legacy digital asset revenue continued to shrink as a percentage of total sales, reinforcing Terawulf’s aggressive pivot toward hosting artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure.

Despite the revenue growth, Terawulf faced mounting pressure on its operating profitability during the quarter. According to financial results released Nov. 6, the company’s operating loss widened to $88.2 million from $24.7 million in the corresponding quarter of 2025.

The widening loss was driven largely by a surge in selling, general, and administrative expenses as Terawulf expanded corporate operations, hired additional technical and electrical personnel, and advanced its multigigawatt development pipeline. Interest expenses also rose significantly year over year, reflecting a larger debt burden and convertible notes used to finance its capital-intensive expansion. Total costs and expenses more than doubled to $164.5 million from $75.3 million in the third quarter of 2025.

Terawulf Expands AI Infrastructure Footprint

Terawulf’s widening operating losses and rising costs reflect its extensive infrastructure expansion across several major data center campuses. Its Lake Mariner facility had 102 megawatts (MW) of operational IT capacity as of Sept. 30, with another 336 MW under construction at an estimated cost of $8 million to $10 million per MW.

At its Justified Campus, the company secured a 20-year lease agreement with Anthropic representing approximately $19 billion in contracted revenue, supported by a Google credit backstop for project financing. Meanwhile, Terawulf expanded its Muskie Campus in Kentucky to 1 gigawatt (GW) of contracted power capacity, strengthening its long-term development pipeline.

To support its capital-intensive expansion and manage rising costs, Terawulf ended the third quarter with approximately $2.4 billion in cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash. The company also completed the sale of its 50.1% stake in the Abernathy Joint Venture, receiving $250 million in upfront cash consideration, with additional payments expected. It also increased commitments under its revolving credit agreement to $400 million.

IREN’s AI Pivot Highlights Industrywide Shift

Terawulf’s transition mirrors a broader shift among publicly traded bitcoin miners seeking to capitalize on growing demand for AI computing infrastructure. Nasdaq-listed IREN, another bitcoin mining company pivoting toward AI cloud services, reported a sharp decline in mining revenue for the quarter ended Sept. 30.

According to its quarterly filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, IREN generated $28 million in bitcoin mining revenue, down 58% from $67 million in the previous quarter and 88% from $233 million a year earlier. Bitcoin production plunged to 402 BTC from 2,039 BTC a year earlier, while its average operating hashrate fell to 8.8 exahash per second (EH/s) from 45.3 EH/s.

IREN held no bitcoin on its balance sheet at the end of September, reflecting its practice of selling mined bitcoin daily. The company expects to substantially complete its transition from bitcoin mining to AI cloud operations by Dec. 31, 2026, with only minimal mining activity continuing through 2027.

The shift has already transformed IREN’s revenue mix. Its quarterly revenue climbed 66% sequentially to $228 million, driven by approximately $200 million in AI cloud revenue, up 182% from the previous quarter. The company also narrowed its net loss to $263 million from $684 million, while adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization rose to $66 million from $19 million.

IREN reported total assets of $20.6 billion, including $6 billion in data center assets, supported by customer agreements involving Nvidia, Microsoft and 13 other customers.

However, the transition has not insulated mining companies from broader market volatility. IREN shares fell 17% Nov. 5 to close at $18.03 amid a sell-off in AI and technology stocks. Despite the decline, analysts remain upbeat and maintain a price target of $55.

title: Here’s what happened in crypto today
summary: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.
content:
Today in crypto, the US Treasury moved to cut MEXC off from the US financial system over alleged illicit transactions, questions remain about Binance’s hot wallet safeguards following its $6.3 billion hack, and other crypto exchanges are disclosing their cold storage reserves to reassure customers.

US Treasury cuts off MEXC over alleged $16B in illicit transactions

The US Department of Treasury on Friday issued an order to cut cryptocurrency exchange MEXC Global off from the US’ financial system after accusing it of facilitating at least $16 billion in transactions linked to sanctions evasion, cybercrime and other illicit activity.

The Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) asserted that MEXC handled transactions involving sanctioned groups in Iran, Russia and North Korea between May 2021 and May 2026. This included around $1.5 billion in transactions linked to Russian sanctions evasion, according to the official press release.

The order effectively bans US financial institutions from processing money transfers involving MEXC and will take effect 30 days after it is published in the Federal Register. 

“Financial institutions cannot have it both ways: Either you support the Iranian regime, or you have access to the U.S. financial system,” said Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent. “Treasury will continue to sever the Iranian regime’s economic lifelines and thwart its desperate attempts to circumvent U.S. sanctions using digital assets.”

The action is part of Operation Economic Outcast, a US Treasury campaign launched in August with aims to cut off financial entities that help Iran evade sanctions.

According to DefiLlama, the exchange held about $4.48 billion in total assets as of Friday. Cointelegraph contacted MEXC for comment but had not received a response by publication.

Binance’s $6.3B hack leaves questions over hot wallet safeguards

Binance’s $6.3 billion security incident has left unanswered questions about how the exchange managed its hot wallets and limited the amount attackers could access.

Binance co-CEO Richard Teng said on Oct. 30 that the attack affected the exchange’s own hot wallet. Most customer assets were held in offline cold storage and moved to hot wallets only when users requested withdrawals.

Wallet balances offer only a partial picture of an exchange’s exposure to an attack. Public blockchain records can show funds moving but cannot establish the internal controls governing those transfers, CertiK analyst Jonathan Riss told Cointelegraph.

In its initial report Tuesday, Binance said attackers accessed an internal wallet-signing service to move funds outside its normal withdrawal process. Binance said some technical details would remain confidential to prevent further attacks.

Crypto exchanges tout cold storage ratios after Binance attack

Crypto exchanges were quick to reassure users following the attack on Binance’s hot wallet infrastructure last week, with several companies disclosing how they divide assets between cold storage and internet-connected hot wallets this week. 

Crypto exchange Gate on Thursday launched a “Proof of Security” (PoSEC) framework, reporting that 88.26% of its total assets were in cold storage and 11.74% in hot wallets. It claims its cold storage could cover 104.58% of customer assets even if its hot wallets were completely drained.

“By publicly disclosing the distribution of assets between platform cold storage and hot wallets, PoSEC provides visibility into asset storage structures and their ability to cover potential losses under extreme scenarios,” Gate said. It noted the data is still undergoing independent review by a third-party audit firm.

Threat actors attacked Binance’s hot-wallet infrastructure last week, stealing approximately $6.36 billion, most of it in about 20 minutes, according to TRM Labs. Binance CEO Richard Teng said the “vast majority” of user assets are held in cold wallets, but the company has not provided a precise split.

title: Nigeria Erects Strict Stablecoin Wall, Demanding $11M Local Subsidiaries for US Dollar Tokens
summary:
Nigeria has adopted regulations for non-security virtual assets that make it one of the most restrictive stablecoin market-access regimes currently in force. 
According to the document, published by the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), foreign issuers must build a locally licensed operation before mak...
content:
2026-11-06T23:54:00.000+02:00

Friday, 06/11/2026 | 21:54 GMT by Tanya Chepkova

  • Dollar stablecoins can serve Nigerian retail users only through a locally incorporated, CBN-licensed issuer.
  • Stablecoin payments or remittances might require separate CBN approval.

Nigeria has adopted regulations for non-security virtual assets that make it one of the most restrictive stablecoin market-access regimes currently in force.

According to the document, published by the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), foreign issuers must build a locally licensed operation before making their tokens available to retail customers. New rules combine local incorporation, token-level approval, capital requirements and separate permissions for payment functions.

The regulations, effective from 5 November, apply to overseas companies targeting Nigerian users even when those businesses have no physical presence in the country.

Dollar Stablecoins Need a Nigerian Issuer

The CBN divides stablecoins into two categories. Class 1 covers tokens pegged to the naira, while Class 2 applies to those referencing foreign currencies, such as dollar-backed tokens USDT or USDC.

Foreign issuers are effectively cut off from the local retail customers until they establish a Nigerian company, obtain Class 2 issuer licence, and CBN approval for their tokens

That local company must maintain at least NGN15 billion (approximately $11.1 million) in paid-up capital and provide operational liquidity for redemptions in Nigeria.

Tokens must be fully backed by assets denominated in their reference currency, with an additional 2% buffer. The issuer must also appoint a Nigerian bank to process local redemption requests.

Stablecoin Payments Require a Second Approval

The new framework divides oversight: the SEC remains responsible for trading and investment-related custody, while the CBN controls payment and money-transfer services.

An SEC-licensed crypto platform can therefore list a stablecoin or hold it for trading clients. However, for customer transfers, merchant payments, remittances, payment gateways or stored-value products separate CBN authorisation is required.

These permissions are activity-specific. A company authorised for custody or exchange cannot assume that the same approval covers a P2P service or cross-border payments.

Providers of these non-issuance services must also maintain at least NGN1 billion, or approximately $741,000, in additional capital. Moreover, a SEC-regulated platform cannot use the same funds to satisfy both regulators’ requirements.

Conversions between naira and a foreign-currency stablecoin may require an authorised foreign-exchange channel, transaction reporting and specific CBN approval.

This regulatory approach creates a layered model in which the token, its issuer and each payment function must all receive the appropriate permission.

Nigeria Is Already One of Africa’s Largest Crypto Markets

The rules apply to a market where cryptoassets are used for more than speculative trading. Stablecoins provide Nigerian citizens and businesses with access to dollar-denominated value and an alternative channel for cross-border payments when conventional transfers are expensive or foreign currency is difficult to obtain.

Chainalysis estimated that Nigeria recorded $38.1 billion in crypto activity between July 2025 and June 2026, slightly below South Africa’s $39.3 billion. Nigeria also ranked third in the company’s global grassroots adoption index, which measures patterns of everyday use rather than absolute transaction volume.

Stablecoin activity through peer-to-peer channels increased more than sixfold between 2022 and 2026, from $2.3 billion to $14.6 billion, according to the same study. This combination of dollar demand, cross-border use and growing domestic distribution helps explain the structure of the CBN regime.

The regulator is permitting stablecoins, but wants their issuance, conversion and payment functions to pass through locally supervised companies and approved financial channels.

Existing operators have 180 days to apply, but may continue only at their current scale during the transition. They must register within 30 days and begin supervisory reporting within 60 days, making expansion dependent on securing the new approvals.

title: US Treasury Blacklists MEXC Over $16B in Alleged Illicit Crypto Activity
summary: The U.S. Treasury Department has ordered American financial institutions to stop processing transactions involving cryptocurrency exchange MEXC Global, accusing the platform of facilitating at least $16 billion in illicit financial activity tied to sanctions evasion, cybercrime, and other illegal op...
content:
The U.S. Treasury Department has ordered American financial institutions to stop processing transactions involving cryptocurrency exchange MEXC Global, accusing the platform of facilitating at least $16 billion in illicit financial activity tied to sanctions evasion, cybercrime, and other illegal operations.

Key Takeaways

  • FinCEN ordered U.S. financial institutions to stop processing transactions involving crypto exchange MEXC Global over alleged illicit financial activity.
  • The U.S. Treasury accused MEXC of facilitating transactions tied to sanctions evasion, cybercrime, and sanctioned entities in Iran, Russia, and North Korea between 2021 and 2026.
  • The order further isolates MEXC from the U.S. financial system, following previous sanctions against crypto platforms linked to Iran and Russia.

Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) announced the action Friday as part of Operation Economic Outcast, President Donald Trump’s administration’s campaign to isolate Iran from international financial markets. The order effectively cuts MEXC off from the U.S. financial system and takes effect 30 days after publication in the Federal Register.

According to Treasury, MEXC processed at least $16 billion in suspicious transactions between May 2021 and May 2026, including funds linked to sanctioned entities in Iran, Russia, and North Korea.

“Financial institutions cannot have it both ways: Either you support the Iranian regime, or you have access to the U.S. financial system,” Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said in the announcement.

Treasury described MEXC as one of the world’s 20 largest cryptocurrency exchanges, handling more than $1 billion in daily transactions and holding approximately $5 billion in reserves as of September. The exchange offers access to more than 3,000 cryptocurrencies and tokenized assets.

Despite maintaining customer verification and anti-money laundering policies, MEXC allegedly failed to prevent transactions involving sanctioned individuals and organizations.

Treasury said approximately $1.5 billion in transactions were connected to Russian sanctions evasion, including $232 million transferred directly to or from entities sanctioned by the United States, European Union, and United Kingdom.

The exchange allegedly continued processing transactions involving Garantex, a Russian cryptocurrency platform sanctioned by the United States in 2022, and its successor Grinex as recently as June 2026.

MEXC also purportedly processed at least $26 million benefiting Russia’s sanctioned A7 network and nearly $200 million connected to the A7A5 stablecoin, which U.S. officials have identified as a tool for circumventing financial restrictions.

Iranian activity accounted for another significant portion of the transactions. Treasury said MEXC sent or received approximately $1 billion directly involving more than 40 Iranian cryptocurrency exchanges over the five-year period. Another $22 million in transactions involved Iran’s sanctioned central bank, Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, and its Qods Force, according to the announcement.

Treasury Takes Aim at Sanctions-Evading Exchanges

The latest action follows a broader U.S. crackdown on cryptocurrency infrastructure allegedly supporting sanctioned governments.

As previously reported by Bitcoin.com News, Treasury expanded its sanctions authority in August to cover Iran’s digital asset sector under Operation Economic Outcast, exposing foreign cryptocurrency businesses to potential penalties for supporting the country’s financial networks.

In September, U.S. authorities also sanctioned Iranian cryptocurrency exchange Bitbank, alleging that financier Babak Zanjani used the platform to transfer hundreds of millions of dollars in bitcoin to the Revolutionary Guard.

MEXC had already begun withdrawing from certain international markets. Bitcoin.com News reported in October that the exchange was winding down services for users in Russia and Belarus, citing global compliance requirements amid tightening European sanctions.

Friday’s action goes further by restricting MEXC’s access to American financial institutions, rather than simply limiting services in particular countries.

FinCEN issued the order under Section 9714 of the Combating Russian Money Laundering Act. U.S. financial institutions will be prohibited from transmitting funds to or from MEXC once the restrictions take effect, with potential civil or criminal penalties for violations.

title: U.S. Treasury Cuts Off MEXC From U.S. Financial System Over Alleged $16 Billion in Illicit Flows
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

U.S. Treasury Cuts Off MEXC From U.S. Financial System Over Alleged $16 Billion in Illicit Flows
FinCEN issued a final order under section 9714(a) that will bar U.S. financial institutions from sending or receiving funds with MEXC Global 30 days after Federal Register publication, ...
content:
The U.S. Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network issued a final order Friday that will cut offshore exchange MEXC Global off from the American banking system over alleged links to sanctions evasion by Iran, North Korea and Russia, the department said.

FinCEN’s order, published as a PDF pending Federal Register placement, finds MEXC a “primary money laundering concern in connection with Russian illicit finance” under section 9714(a) of the Combating Russian Money Laundering Act. Thirty days after that Register notice, covered U.S. financial institutions will be barred from any funds transfer — including convertible virtual currency — to or from MEXC.

Reuters reported the same cut-off Friday afternoon. Treasury framed the move as part of Operation Economic Outcast. It is not an OFAC sanctions designation: the order says it does not rewrite Bank Secrecy Act duties or OFAC rules, and it is a FinCEN funds-transmittal ban rather than a Section 311 proposed rulemaking.

Treasury alleges MEXC facilitated at least $16 billion in illicit flows from May 2021 through May 2026, including nearly $1.5 billion tied to Russian sanctions evasion and about $22 million linked to Iran’s Central Bank and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps’ Qods Force. The platform was still processing trades with sanctioned Garantex and successor Grinex as recently as June 2026, more than four years after OFAC designated Garantex, the release says.

What the order does — and when

The order, signed by FinCEN Deputy Director Jimmy L. Kirby, covers MEXC Global and named affiliates operating outside the United States, including Seychelles-incorporated MEXC Global Ltd / MX Global Ltd, Estonia’s MEXC Estonia OÜ, Switzerland’s GIDA Technology AG and the U.K.’s MXC Global Ltd, plus successors. Covered institutions face civil or criminal penalties for willful violations.

Until the Federal Register publishes the notice, the 30-day clock has not started. As of Friday evening eastern time the Register’s public index still showed no MEXC document, matching the order’s own cover note that publication is pending.

Background on MEXC

Founded in 2018 and formerly branded MXC, MEXC ranks among the world’s 20 largest centralized crypto venues by volume. Treasury puts daily turnover above $1 billion and reserves near $5 billion as of mid-2026, with access claimed across more than 170 countries. The exchange already lists the United States as a prohibited jurisdiction in its user terms, so Friday’s action mainly hits any remaining dollar rails, banking partners and counterparties that still touch U.S. institutions.

Regulators elsewhere have been circling for years. The U.K. Financial Conduct Authority put MEXC Global Ltd on its warning list in March 2024 as unauthorized. Hong Kong’s Securities and Futures Commission warned the same month that the platform was marketing to local investors without a licence. Seychelles’ Financial Services Authority said in May 2026 it took action against MX Global Ltd for unlicensed virtual-asset operations — footnoted in FinCEN’s order.

Those compliance gaps matter because the illicit-flow thesis is specific, not guilt by association. Beyond Russia, FinCEN cites about $1 billion in direct traffic with more than 40 Iranian crypto exchangers, nearly $26 million with the OFAC-sanctioned A7 sanctions-evasion network, and almost $200 million tied to the A7A5 stablecoin. DPRK facilitators and cybercrime flows are also alleged. MEXC has not issued a public response to the Friday order; its main X account kept posting marketing content through the afternoon.

Why it matters for bitcoin markets

Practically, once the order bites, U.S. banks, money transmitters and other covered firms cannot move dollars or crypto to MEXC wallets or accounts. Offshore users may keep trading peer-to-peer, but dollar on-ramps and any bank that still clears for MEXC become legal risk. The template tracks earlier 9714 cut-offs of venues such as Bitzlato, and it lands beside a busy sanctions week that has already seen North Korea crypto designations, an Iranian exchange action, and Russia’s push to put bitcoin trading on the Moscow Exchange.

Whether MEXC contests the finding, seeks an exemption, or quietly reroutes liquidity is the open question. For now the paper trail is clear: a final FinCEN order under 9714(a), a 30-day fuse after Federal Register publication, and Treasury’s claim of at least $16 billion in illicit volume sitting behind the cut-off.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: US Treasury cuts off MEXC over alleged $16B in illicit transactions
summary: The US Treasury bureau FinCEN on Friday ordered US financial institutions to stop processing transfers involving MEXC Global.
content:
Latest NewsPublishedNov 6, 2026

The US Treasury bureau FinCEN on Friday ordered US financial institutions to stop processing transfers involving MEXC Global.

The US Department of Treasury on Friday issued an order to cut cryptocurrency exchange MEXC Global off from the US’ financial system after accusing it of facilitating at least $16 billion in transactions linked to sanctions evasion, cybercrime and other illicit activity.

The Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) asserted that MEXC handled transactions involving sanctioned groups in Iran, Russia and North Korea between May 2021 and May 2026. This included around $1.5 billion in transactions linked to Russian sanctions evasion, according to the official press release.

The order effectively bans US financial institutions from processing money transfers involving MEXC and will take effect 30 days after it is published in the Federal Register. 

“Financial institutions cannot have it both ways: Either you support the Iranian regime, or you have access to the U.S. financial system,” said Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent. “Treasury will continue to sever the Iranian regime’s economic lifelines and thwart its desperate attempts to circumvent U.S. sanctions using digital assets.”

The action is part of Operation Economic Outcast, a US Treasury campaign launched in August with aims to cut off financial entities that help Iran evade sanctions.

According to DefiLlama, the exchange held about $4.48 billion in total assets as of Friday. Cointelegraph contacted MEXC for comment but had not received a response by publication.

title: Gnosis Pay breach exposes card details, personal data and crypto wallet information
summary: The crypto debit card provider said customer funds remained safe despite the exposure of sensitive financial and personal information.
content:
Crypto-linked Visa debit card provider Gnosis Pay disclosed a security breach on Friday that exposed customers’ payment card details, home addresses and cryptocurrency wallet addresses.

Gnosis Pay said it detected unauthorized access to its legacy consumer card system on Nov. 3 and began containing the breach within two hours. The company said customer funds and its separate enterprise platform, which powers white-label card programs, were unaffected.

According to breach notifications reviewed by Cointelegraph, the company identified exposed information including full payment card numbers, expiration dates, CVV codes, customer names, home addresses and wallet addresses linked to affected accounts. The compromised data also included email addresses, phone numbers, nationalities and, in some cases, banking details such as IBAN and BIC information.

Gnosis Pay customer shares a breach notification detailing exposed personal and financial data. Source: Lefteris Karapetsas

One notification also confirmed that the customer’s card was canceled on Nov. 3, with no suspicious transactions or movement of funds detected.

Gnosis Pay said it replaced compromised security credentials, addressed the vulnerability and made 3D Secure verification mandatory for online payments until the legacy system’s planned retirement on Dec. 20. It also warned customers about phishing attempts using their personal or transaction details and said it was arranging monitoring for potential misuse of the stolen data.

According to data from OpenRate, a third-party platform tracking crypto card activity, Gnosis Pay had around 2,400 daily active cardholders and processed $263,200 in transactions over the previous 24 hours.

The company did not disclose how many customers were affected and did not immediately respond to Cointelegraph’s request for comment.

title: Binance hack is ‘cyber war,’ TRM Labs executive says
summary: TRM Labs executive Ari Redbord called for governments to take offensive action against North Korean hackers following the record $6.3 billion Binance theft.
content:
The $6.3 billion Binance hack sent shockwaves through the crypto industry. Following a series of increasingly severe cybersecurity incidents, the attack on the world’s biggest crypto exchange demonstrated how far state-backed hackers can, and will, go.

TRM Labs, a blockchain intelligence company, was on the front lines of efforts to stop the theft, releasing a report in its aftermath. The firm was early to attribute the attack to the North Korean hacking group, TraitorTrader, citing “indisputable” onchain and offchain evidence. The $1.5 billion hack of Bybit in February 2025 was attributed to the same group. 

Binance said in its postmortem on Nov. 3 that attackers posed as recruiters to plant malware on an engineer’s work computer, then used a compromised internal AI tool to reach its wallet-signing service. 

Ari Redbord, TRM Labs’ global head of policy and government affairs, told Cointelegraph that although the industry’s coordinated response to the attack was unprecedented, “we are only going to see much more of this.” 

Unprecedented response from the industry

The speed and scale of industry’s response to the hack were among the factors that stood out to Redbord.

Tether froze 971.1 million USDt (USDT) tokens just 37 minutes after the main sweep. Combined, stablecoin issuers froze tokens worth about $2.67 billion, according to TRM. “Nothing like that has ever been done before,” Redbord said. “They were able to claw back 40% right out the gate.”

The race to catch stolen funds before hackers can move them offchain is a critical part of defending against such attacks. TRM’s Redbord explained that the Beacon Network, an intelligence-sharing system TRM launched in 2025, allowed companies to coordinate quickly to immobilize the funds before working to seize them. “Normally I see a few Beacon alerts maybe every day. I’ve seen, I don’t know, hundreds or maybe even a thousand Beacon alerts over the last few days,” he said.

Related: Ethereum devs won’t fork Glamsterdam on Hoodi until smart contract risks resolved

The push for coordination comes as Bloomberg reported on Nov. 4 that the T3 Financial Crime Unit, which TRM formed with Tron and Tether in September 2024, disbanded in late August, with sources citing slow responses and poor coordination. Tether said it would continue working with TRM through Beacon.

Although Redbord called for greater coordination, he warned that such efforts may do little to deter future attacks. He noted that North Korea’s Oct. 29 theft was equivalent to roughly a third of the country’s GDP and accounted for half of the $12.5 billion stolen by state-backed hackers since 2017. Even if attackers recover only $1 billion, the potential payoff remains enormous, he argued.

“North Korea will keep doing this as long as it’s effective,” he said.

From defense to offense

Redbord argued that stopping such attacks requires offensive action from governments in response to North Korea’s use of hackers operating as an arm of the state. 

TRM’s capacity gap report found that the gap between attackers and cybersecurity defenders continues to widen, driven by hackers’ early adoption of frontier technologies such as AI. He said law enforcement and compliance teams need AI to find and patch vulnerabilities as quickly as hackers can exploit them.

“Every time North Korea hacks, we should be hacking them back,” he continued, calling for offensive cyber operations and action against laundering networks and banks that hackers use to cash out. “This is cyber war,” he said.

title: Zcash Rises After Upgrade Freezes $16M in ZEC, Establishes Security Reserve
summary: Zcash has activated Network Upgrade 7, which reduces block times from 75 to 25 seconds and will help fuel a long-term security reserve. However, the move also froze about $16 million worth of ZEC that will remain inaccessible in an outdated shielded pool. Zcash Cuts Block Times While Preserving Supp...
content:
Zcash has activated Network Upgrade 7, which reduces block times from 75 to 25 seconds and will help fuel a long-term security reserve. However, the move also froze about $16 million worth of ZEC that will remain inaccessible in an outdated shielded pool.

Key Takeaways

  • Zcash’s NU7 upgrade cuts block times from 75 to 25 seconds while preserving its 21 million ZEC supply cap.
  • Shielded Labs’ new mechanism redirects 60% of Zcash transaction fees to a long-term security reserve.
  • Zcash will begin redistributing reserved ZEC in 2031, while its next halving remains on track for 2028.

Zcash Cuts Block Times While Preserving Supply Cap

Zcash has officially completed its latest network upgrade, Network Upgrade 7 (NU7), activating at block 3,543,405. The major milestone introduces a shift to 25-second block target times alongside the mainnet deployment of the Network Sustainability Mechanism (NSM), designed to address long-term tokenomics and security as block subsidies decline.

With NU7, Zcash transitions block target times from 75 seconds to 25 seconds. To keep total daily ZEC issuance consistent with the existing schedule, the block reward has been proportionally adjusted to 0.52083333 ZEC per block.

The total 21 million supply cap and the timing of the next halving, projected for late 2028 at block 6,132,390, remain completely unchanged. NU7 also officially invalidates Version 4 transactions, freezing the legacy Sprout pool.

That means more than $16 million worth of ZEC (roughly 12,224 ZEC) held in the network’s original Sprout shielded pool is now unspendable, effectively freezing the funds under the new consensus rules. Zcash co-founder Sean Bowe in September described the lingering Sprout pool, which had previously been exit-only, as “pure technical debt” and “a needless security risk for the project.”

The headline economic change in NU7 is the activation of the NSM, developed by Shielded Labs. Building on an idea originally proposed by Nate Wilcox as the “Zcash Posterity Fund,” the NSM addresses a challenge inherited from Bitcoin: securing the network over the long term as mining subsidies taper off.

New Mechanism Redirects Transaction Fees to Security Reserve

Key features of the NSM deployment include redirecting 60% of all transaction fees out of active circulation into the NSM balance, leaving miners with 40%. Gradually those accumulated funds will be reissued starting in 2031 along a smooth curve layered over the halving schedule, rather than burning the ZEC. To further bolster this security reserve, a separate proposal under consideration evaluates contributing an additional 50,000 ZEC directly from the Zcash Community Grants treasury into the NSM.

Emphasizing the long-term focus of the upgrade, Shielded Labs’ Jason McGee noted, “Zcash is money for an infinite civilization, and we’re building for a network that remains secure and sustainable for centuries to come.”

Shielded Labs’ initial design proposed replacing halvings altogether with a smooth issuance curve. While community panels supported the original design, coinholders favored preserving halvings. In response, Shielded Labs adjusted the design to maintain the classic halving cycle while integrating the recycled issuance mechanism.

Writing on X, McGee highlighted this iterative process as a core strength of Zcash’s consensus model, noting that no single entity or individual can unilaterally push changes to the protocol.

The deployment of NU7 represents a key milestone for Shielded Labs alongside ongoing initiatives such as Crosslink and Epoch. While the full economic effects of the NSM will unfold over years and decades, the upgrade lays the groundwork for Zcash’s long-term security as block subsidies continue to decline.

Meanwhile, ZEC appeared to rally on the upgrade finalization, surging from $1,225 to briefly surpass $1,380 even as the broader cryptocurrency market sat nearly even after substantial losses on Thursday. As of this writing, the privacy coin was trading around $1,345, up approximately 8% over the previous 24 hours.

title: US 401(k) proposal leaves door open to altcoins, but hurdles remain
summary: While the proposal doesn’t exclude altcoins and smaller cryptocurrencies, experts say they could face challenges getting into retirement plans.
content:
Smaller cryptocurrencies could become available in US 401(k) retirement plans under a proposed Labor Department rule, but experts say they may face more challenges than Bitcoin (BTC) and Ether (ETH).

The rule reached the White House for final review on Thursday, according to the Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs. It aims to make it easier for retirement plans to offer alternative investments like crypto, while offering more legal protection for employers and plan managers.

The Labor Department’s March proposal neither specifies which digital assets could be included nor sets a minimum market capitalization requirement. However, it does guide retirement plan managers to consider six factors when choosing: performance, fees, liquidity, valuation, benchmarks and complexity.

The proposal could open the door to more cryptocurrencies in retirement plans, however, it does not guarantee they will be offered. And when it comes to smaller tokens, experts say they could face challenges because of their limited history, liquidity and other risks.

Why smaller cryptocurrencies could face challenges

Teresa Goody Guillén, managing partner at Bellementis PLLC, said Bitcoin and Ether are likely to be the first cryptocurrencies offered because of their established markets and investment products. Bitcoin and Ether are the two largest cryptocurrencies by market capitalization, at approximately $1.5 trillion and $273 billion, respectively, according to CoinGecko data as of 20:01 UTC on Nov. 6.

Still, that doesn’t automatically exclude altcoins, she said. Instead, those managing 401(k) plans would need to show that their investment choices are sensible. 

“The real question isn’t which cryptocurrencies regulators pick – it’s whether an investment meets the same standards of prudence, liquidity, valuation and investor protection as any other retirement option,” Guillén said.

She added that while a digital asset’s market cap matters, it shouldn’t be the deciding factor. “Big doesn’t mean suitable, and small doesn’t mean disqualified,” Guillén said. “Digital assets shouldn’t get special treatment, or be excluded because they use different technology.”

Bernardo Brites, co-founder and CEO of Trace Finance, echoed Guillén sentiment, adding: “Run any token through that list and the answer is short. Bitcoin passes clearly. Ether passes; everything else fails on track record or benchmark before a fiduciary ever gets to market cap.”

Brites explained, in this situation, market cap matters only indirectly. “The practical test is simpler: can a plan committee document a daily, reliable price from a regulated wrapper?” he said. “If not, it is not going in.”

ETFs could come before direct crypto holdings

While the Labor Department’s proposal does not limit crypto investments to exchange-traded funds (ETFs) or managed funds, experts said those products will likely be offered before direct crypto holdings.

“ETFs and managed funds will likely come first because they fit existing custody and recordkeeping systems,” Guillén said. Whereas holding cryptocurrencies directly would raise additional concerns about storage, cybersecurity and pricing, Guillén said. Still, she added that those risks should not automatically rule them out.

Brites also expects crypto investments to become available gradually. He said existing brokerage options would likely come first, followed by standalone ETFs and funds that include small amounts of crypto.

He expects some crypto investment options to become available in 2027, followed by ETFs at larger employers later that year. Crypto could become more widely available in retirement funds by 2028, he said.

“The rule changes the legal risk, not the plumbing, and the plumbing is slower,” Brites said. “White House review can take up to ninety days, then publication, then an effective date typically sixty days later.”

Legal uncertainties remain

Brites further explained that legal uncertainty could also slow adoption. The proposal would offer retirement plan managers some protection from lawsuits, but it would not prevent them from being sued over their investment decisions.

He also warned that future administrations could reverse the rule, a possibility that could make employers hesitant to add crypto to long-term retirement plans.

“The 2022 guidance was reversed in 2025; a fiduciary signing a ten-year plan design has to consider that this rule could be reversed too,” he said. “And with courts giving less deference to agencies, how much weight the safe harbor carries in litigation is itself unsettled.”

title: MEXC Refers French Clients to Kraken as Its EU Retreat Widens
summary:

London's trading industry is coming home!
The Kraken announcement follows MEXC’s October 28 notice that it would gradually stop serving users linked to...

2026-11-06T22:02:00.000+02:00

Friday, 06/11/2026 | 20:02 GMT by Tanya Chepkova

  • Customers who choose to switch must open a new account and transfer their assets themselves.
  • Trading restrictions begin on November 18, with withdrawals closing on March 5, 2027.

MEXC will refer eligible French customers to Kraken, extending a transition arrangement the two crypto exchanges previously used in the Netherlands.

London's trading industry is coming home!

The Kraken announcement follows MEXC’s October 28 notice that it would gradually stop serving users linked to France. MEXC attributed the decision to regulatory alignment.

The referral does not automatically move customer accounts, balances or trading positions, according to the announcement. French users choosing Kraken will need to open a separate account, complete KYC procedures and transfer their assets themselves.

Kraken’s crypto services in France are provided by Payward Europe Solutions Limited, which is authorised under MiCA in Ireland and listed by the AMF as permitted to serve French clients.

Trading Restrictions Begin in November

MEXC has divided affected customers into four groups based on their account and identity verification information. The first group enters the wind-down process on November 18, 2026, followed by others on December 10, December 31 and January 22, 2027.

Once an account enters wind-down mode, the customer cannot open or increase positions, make new spot purchases or deposit additional funds. Existing positions can still be reduced or closed, liabilities repaid and assets withdrawn.

MEXC plans to close any remaining positions automatically at 00:00 on January 22, 2027. For customers in the fourth group, that is also when wind-down restrictions begin, so they must close positions by January 21 to avoid automatic closure.

All affected accounts move to withdrawal-only status on January 25. Withdrawals through MEXC close at 00:00 on March 5, 2027, rather than remaining available throughout that day.

France Extends an Earlier EU Exit

MEXC previously stopped serving customers in the Netherlands and recommended regulated alternatives, including Kraken and Bybit EU. Customers who chose another exchange had to open a new account; their MEXC accounts were not migrated.

The French withdrawal also follows an earlier regulatory warning. The AMF added www.mexc.com to its blacklist on June 4, 2024, and included the platform in a public warning the following day about websites offering digital-asset services without the required authorisation.

MEXC has named Kraken as the custodian for assets left by Dutch customers after offboarding, a separate arrangement that does not require them to open a Kraken account.

For France, MEXC says assets remaining after the withdrawal deadline will go to a regulated custodian, but it has not identified the company or explained how customers will later claim those holdings.

title: LuqEE Simplifies Solo Bitcoin and Bitcoin Cash Mining
summary: Buying and operating an ASIC miner remains a substantial barrier to solo Bitcoin mining. LuqEE offers another approach: time-based access to professionally hosted mining hardware for Bitcoin (BTC) and Bitcoin Cash (BCH), without the need to purchase or maintain a mining rig. The model has already pr...
content:
Buying and operating an ASIC miner remains a substantial barrier to solo Bitcoin mining. LuqEE offers another approach: time-based access to professionally hosted mining hardware for Bitcoin (BTC) and Bitcoin Cash (BCH), without the need to purchase or maintain a mining rig.

The model has already produced a public record of block discoveries. On October 22, 2026, LuqEE reported a 100th solo block find, identified as Bitcoin Cash block #974,046. The platform’s public ledger listed 103 block discoveries by November 3.

Solo Bitcoin mining without a personal rig

A conventional home mining setup requires more than hardware. Mining equipment draws electricity, produces heat and noise, and demands suitable space, cooling and maintenance. LuqEE places those operational requirements with hosted facilities while giving customers access to defined amounts of processing capacity through a subscription.

According to the company, LuqEE operates industrial ASIC equipment in U.S.-based facilities. A scheduling system allocates fractions of machine time across accounts, delivering mining power in intervals rather than assigning a dedicated rig to each subscription. The platform describes subscription tiers through an average hash rate, a measure of the computing capacity directed toward mining.

That distinction defines the service. Customers purchase access to mining capacity, not ownership of equipment. The platform handles physical operations, while customers select a plan, register a public payout wallet address and review activity through a mobile-friendly dashboard. LuqEE also provides hash rate information and mining logs, allowing participants to follow the service without managing hardware directly.

How solo mining payouts work

Solo mining differs from pooled mining arrangements that distribute smaller rewards among many participants. When allocated hashing capacity solves an eligible block, the relevant solo mining pool directs the available block reward, after applicable pool fees, to the registered miner’s wallet. LuqEE states that the platform does not hold private wallet keys or take custody of block rewards.

No successful block means no block reward from that solo mining attempt. Network difficulty, the amount of computing power and the duration of an allocation all affect the possibility of a discovery. None of those factors creates a guaranteed payout, profit or recovery of subscription costs.

For account setup, LuqEE requests a public receiving address rather than a private wallet key. Supported pools apply relevant payout rules when a miner finds a qualifying block.

Public records show reported block discoveries

LuqEE maintains a public record of reported Bitcoin and Bitcoin Cash solo block discoveries. The ledger lists miner handles, block numbers, timestamps and links to blockchain explorers and mining pool profiles. Those references allow individual entries to be checked against public network information.

The October milestone offers a specific example. The public record identifies Bitcoin Cash block #974,046, dated October 22, 2026, as the 100th reported find. Subsequent entries include further BCH blocks in late October and early November. The records document activity associated with the service, but the results do not establish typical outcomes for subscribers.

The difference matters. Repeated miner handles appear in the ledger, so the block count does not equal the number of people who found blocks. A historical list also cannot forecast the outcome of a future mining session. LuqEE’s audit information and pool links offer visibility into reported activity while preserving the uncertainty inherent in solo mining.

What hosted access changes

Hosted access removes the requirement to purchase an ASIC machine, arrange a home installation or manage equipment upkeep. The approach can make the practical side of solo Bitcoin mining more approachable, particularly for participants seeking exposure to the mining process rather than a hardware project.

However, a simpler setup does not reduce blockchain mining to a predictable income stream. Mining difficulty changes, infrastructure can experience interruptions and an entire paid session may end without a block. Subscription costs remain relevant regardless of the result. LuqEE’s published risk disclosure also notes that access may depend on local rules and service availability.

LuqEE’s central proposition is therefore operational rather than financial: hosted ASIC capacity, direct wallet settlement for qualifying block discoveries and a public record that supports independent review. Current mining plans, block records and service terms are available on the official LuqEE website.

title: Magnificent 7 Stocks Lose $1 Trillion, but Their Shift Is Just Beginning: Devere CEO
summary: The Magnificent 7’s $1 trillion loss did not end the case for technology stocks, Devere CEO Nigel Green said. He predicted a more selective market as investors demanded evidence that artificial intelligence spending was generating revenue. Green Predicts a Shift in How Investors Buy Tech Nigel Green...
content:
The Magnificent 7’s $1 trillion loss did not end the case for technology stocks, Devere CEO Nigel Green said. He predicted a more selective market as investors demanded evidence that artificial intelligence spending was generating revenue.

Key Takeaways

  • Tesla and Nvidia each sank more than 9% on Thursday, Nov. 5, while Apple slipped just 1.5%.
  • Green says investors will now grill each giant on customers and power.
  • The Devere CEO sees capitulation in the sell-off and expects a more durable run.

Green Predicts a Shift in How Investors Buy Tech

Nigel Green, CEO of financial advisory firm Devere Group, assessed the Magnificent 7’s loss of more than $1 trillion on Nov. 5 in comments sent to Bitcoin.com News on Nov. 6. He argued that their established businesses supported continued growth. Green stated:

“Wiping $1 trillion off the tech super pack in a day naturally makes people ask whether its reign is over. The answer is no.”

The Magnificent 7 comprises major U.S. technology and technology-related stocks: Apple, Microsoft, Nvidia, Amazon, Google parent company Alphabet, Meta, and Tesla. Their businesses span cloud computing, chips, smartphones, advertising, and online retail.

Looking ahead, he explained: “What’s finished is the habit of buying all seven as one trade. From here, each will be judged on its own numbers, and many investors will see this sell-off as a chance to buy the dip.”

Uneven Losses Put Company Results in Focus

On Nov. 5, Tesla sank 10.77% and Nvidia fell 9.26%, while Apple declined 1.53%. Microsoft lost 3.58%, Meta dropped 3.96%, Amazon slid 2.19%, and Alphabet fell 2.20%. Green said:

“Even in a panic, investors picked their targets. The market has started sorting the Magnificent 7 into stronger and weaker hands.”

Across Wall Street, the damage included the S&P 500 losing 4.4% and the Nasdaq 5.5%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 1,833 points. All 11 S&P 500 sectors closed lower. AI stocks came under pressure on concerns that Democratic victories in the midterm elections could lead to moratoriums on data centers.

By about 9:42 a.m. EST on Nov. 6, Nvidia had rebounded 6.9%, while Tesla gained 2.8%, Meta rose 2.5%, Alphabet added 2.3%, and Amazon advanced 1.1%. Apple and Microsoft remained lower, down 1.3% and 1.1%, respectively. Bitcoin traded near $75,249 on Nov. 6 after touching $74,762. It was about 11.3% below the $84,843 level reached in late October.

The cryptocurrency had also retreated during the Nov. 5 session. Michael Saylor’s comparison of market losses put bitcoin’s decline at about 5% on Nov. 5, alongside the sharper fall in the Nasdaq. His figures showed that the downturn reached digital assets as well as technology shares.

Financing costs complicated the outlook for AI infrastructure. Bitfinex’s analysis of technology financing on Nov. 2 highlighted growing concerns about borrowing costs and increasing reliance on credit to fund capital spending. The assessment added a financing consideration to Green’s emphasis on evaluating individual businesses.

AI Revenue and Power Supplies Shape Green’s Outlook

Customer ownership, secured electricity supplies, and revenue from AI spending were Green’s proposed tests for technology companies. Calls for restrictions on data centers also created uncertainty for infrastructure expansion, including projects involving bitcoin miners. These proposals placed construction approvals alongside financing and power availability among the considerations facing developers.

The Nov. 5 selling showed signs of capitulation, in Green’s assessment. He pointed to a spike in the VIX, which measures expected S&P 500 volatility over the next 30 days, and widespread share declines as indications that forced sellers could be clearing positions. While anticipating further volatility, the executive maintained that demand for computing power continued to grow.

His longer-term forecast centered on a possible change in the group’s leadership. He stated: “Corrections like this squeeze out excess and reward discipline. The super pack will likely keep leading the AI boom, though perhaps with a different pecking order at the top.” Green added:

“A sharper, more selective market should make the next stage of its run far more durable than the last.”

title: Warsaw Stock Exchange Taps XTB to Bring Foreign Retail Investors to Polish Stocks
summary:
Warsaw-listed shares are now open to XTB S.A.'s clients across the European Union without a separate request, the broker and the Warsaw Stock Exchange (GPW) said today (Friday). The two called it a pilot.
Until October, only XTB clients in Poland had automatic access to Warsaw-listed instruments on ...
content:
2026-11-06T21:10:38.310+02:00

Friday, 06/11/2026 | 19:10 GMT by Damian Chmiel

  • EU clients of the broker can now buy Warsaw-listed shares without the extra application needed until October.
  • Domestic brokerage accounts topped 3 million in September, and 1.285 million of them sit at XTB.

Warsaw-listed shares are now open to XTB S.A.'s clients across the European Union without a separate request, the broker and the Warsaw Stock Exchange (GPW) said today (Friday). The two called it a pilot.

Until October, only XTB clients in Poland had automatic access to Warsaw-listed instruments on its platform. Retail investors elsewhere needed an extra application first.

That route was used by clients in France, the Czech Republic, Slovakia, the UK, Portugal, Romania and Spain, according to the release.

The exchange 's retail growth has so far been counted in domestic accounts. The Central Securities Depository of Poland (KDPW) counted more than 3 million brokerage accounts at the end of September, 1.285 million of them at XTB, up from 2,856,520 accounts in May, FM Intelligence data show.

London's trading industry is coming home!

A Polish Firm With a Foreign Client Base

XTB brings the exchange a client base already split between Poland and abroad. Poland generated 54.4% of XTB's 2025 revenue, as FinanceMagnates.com reported when Lynx opened a Warsaw office to compete for Polish savers.

XTB says more than 3.2 million people use its investing app. FM Intelligence's FX/CFD heat map shows by country where web traffic to XTB and 97 other retail brokers comes from.

One of its biggest sources of new accounts lies outside the bloc the pilot covers first: Indonesia now trails only Poland by new accounts, XTB Chief Executive Omar Arnaout said last week.

Filip Kaczmarzyk, a member of XTB's management board, said demand for Polish shares already comes from outside the country.

"We also see interest in the Polish market from our foreign clients," Kaczmarzyk said, adding that automatic access removes operational barriers for investors abroad.

He named CD Projekt, Benefit Systems and LPP as examples of Warsaw-listed companies with business in many international markets.

Index Gains Give the Exchange a Pitch

The cooperation runs under a GPW program aimed at exchange members that serve foreign retail investors. XTB will also run information and promotional campaigns about the Polish market, a month after it launched what it calls the biggest ad campaign in its history.

"We want to use their international reach," said Michał Kobza, a member of the Warsaw Stock Exchange's management board, referring to the brokers in the program.

Kobza said a larger share of foreign investors would support liquidity and make Warsaw-listed companies better known abroad.

The exchange pointed to this year's returns. The WIG20 index has risen more than 34% since January and the mWIG40 30%, against less than 13% for the S&P 500 over the same period.

XTB has been listed on the Warsaw exchange since 2016, and last week reported that its third-quarter profit quadrupled from a year earlier. The two gave no date for clients outside the EU.

title: Russia finalizes crypto trading rules ahead of Nov. 17 rollout
summary: The rules allow retail investors to trade BTC, ETH and USDT through regulated intermediaries, with Moscow Exchange planning to launch crypto trading in December.
content:
Russia’s central bank has finalized rules allowing exchanges to offer Bitcoin (BTC), Ether (ETH) and Tether USDt (USDT) to retail investors starting Nov. 17.

Under the rules, non-qualified investors can purchase up to 300,000 rubles (around $3,700) in cryptocurrency annually through each intermediary, including brokers, asset managers and crypto exchange providers. Qualified investors face no purchase limits, but all investors must pass a mandatory test before trading.

The directive builds on legislation signed by Russian President Vladimir Putin on Aug. 4 establishing a regulated cryptocurrency market under central bank oversight.

A week later, on Aug. 11, the Bank of Russia published its draft regulations, identifying BTC, ETH and USDT as eligible for public trading based on market capitalization, average daily trading volume and at least five years of price history on foreign exchanges.

The law took effect Sept. 1, and the Bank of Russia subsequently authorized Sberbank, the country’s largest bank, to offer crypto exchange services in October.

The regulatory developments come as Moscow Exchange, Russia’s largest securities exchange and a publicly traded company, prepares to launch cryptocurrency trading on Dec. 1, initially offering the three cryptocurrencies through pilot transactions.

Russia to restrict peer-to-peer crypto trading

While expanding access to cryptocurrencies through regulated platforms, Russia is also tightening restrictions on transactions outside those channels.

Direct peer-to-peer crypto trading will be prohibited starting July 1, 2027, while transfers from regulated digital accounts to self-custody wallets are already banned, according to the Bank of Russia. The country also maintains a prohibition on using cryptocurrency to pay for goods and services.

title: Bitcoin Magazine Books Opens 333-Copy Genesis Book Collector Edition for 3rd Anniversary
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Bitcoin Magazine Books Opens 333-Copy Genesis Book Collector Edition for 3rd Anniversary
Bitcoin Magazine Books opened a third-anniversary campaign for Aaron van Wirdum's The Genesis Book, capping a hand-signed Collectors Edition at 333 numbered copies.
This post Bitcoin Magazine B...
content:
Bitcoin Magazine Books opened a third-anniversary campaign Friday for Aaron van Wirdum’s The Genesis Book, offering a redesigned Collectors Edition limited to 333 hand-signed, individually numbered hardcovers in an exclusive Genesis Block slipcase.

Each Collectors Edition hardcover is hand-signed and hand-numbered by van Wirdum, the former Bitcoin Magazine editor-in-chief whose book traces the people, projects and ideas that preceded Satoshi Nakamoto’s peer-to-peer cash design. The standard package is priced at $221 and pairs the book with a limited trading card carrying a Certificate of Authenticity, a collector pin, a sticker sheet, the slipcase and a digital package.

Two one-of-one packages sit outside the ordinary number queue. The #1 package is listed at $5,000 and the #21 package at $2,500; each includes the matching numbered copy, a matching one-of-one collector card and the same accessories as the standard collector package.

Standard collector numbers are assigned in purchase order starting at #2 and skipping #21, the campaign FAQ says. Once preorders close, the signed Genesis print run will not be reproduced.

What ships with the anniversary editions

Beside the signed run, Bitcoin Magazine Books is selling a Premium Edition hardcover for $160 with foil stamping, a ribbon marker, stained page edges and custom endsheets. That edition is not limited, signed, numbered or slipcased, and it does not include the collector accessories or digital files.

A standalone Digital Package at $9.99 delivers the ebook in EPUB and the audiobook in MP4 immediately after purchase, independent of whether the physical campaign clears its funding bar.

Physical collector and premium orders are scheduled to ship in calendar year 2027.

Van Wirdum, who discovered bitcoin in 2013 and later led Bitcoin Magazine‘s editorial desk, frames The Genesis Book as a history of computer scientists, privacy activists and heterodox economists who chased government-independent digital money long before the 2008 white paper — from early cypherpunk culture through experiments such as David Chaum’s ecash, Wei Dai’s b-money, Adam Back’s Hashcash and Hal Finney’s reusable proof of work.

Store images for the slipcase and accessories are artistic renderings; the campaign page notes that color, materials and finishes may vary in production. The campaign is operated by BTC Inc., which publishes Bitcoin Magazine.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: US Treasury and Fed Abandon Plan to Track Smaller Bitcoin, Crypto Transfers
summary: The U.S. Treasury Department and the Federal Reserve are withdrawing a proposal to expand information collection for international crypto transfers as small as $250. The decision preserves the existing $3,000 threshold as officials reassess rules proposed in 2020. Treasury and Fed Drop Proposed $250...
content:
The U.S. Treasury Department and the Federal Reserve are withdrawing a proposal to expand information collection for international crypto transfers as small as $250. The decision preserves the existing $3,000 threshold as officials reassess rules proposed in 2020.

Key Takeaways

  • The withdrawal is scheduled to take effect upon publication Nov. 9.
  • Commenters challenged compliance costs and risks to personal information.
  • Comparable amendments would require another public comment opportunity.

Treasury and Fed Drop Proposed $250 Transfer Threshold

The U.S. Treasury Department’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) and the Federal Reserve Board filed a joint withdrawal notice on Nov. 6, abandoning plans to lower certain international transfer thresholds from $3,000 to $250. The withdrawal is scheduled to take effect upon publication Nov. 9. Referring to the notice of proposed rulemaking (NPRM), a formal proposal inviting public comment, the agencies stated:

“The Agencies will not take further action on this NPRM.”

Under the proposed international transfer requirements, covered banks and nonbank financial institutions would have collected and retained information on smaller payments beginning or ending outside the United States. FinCEN’s Travel Rule would also have required specified information to accompany those payments between institutions. Domestic transfers would have retained the $3,000 threshold.

Separate cryptocurrency provisions in the proposal addressed both domestic and cross-border transactions. They would have explicitly covered convertible virtual currencies, meaning digital value equivalent to or substituting for conventional currency. The provisions also covered digital assets with legal tender status to a recipient.

Commenters Raised Compliance Costs and Privacy Objections

Nearly 3,000 comments reached the agencies from banks, money services businesses, trade associations, individuals, and others, with a significant majority consisting of substantially similar form letters. Respondents generally opposed the lower threshold, citing costs for smaller institutions and risks from retaining more personal information. Some warned of disrupted overseas remittances or favored a higher threshold to reflect inflation since 1995.

Views differed on explicitly incorporating cryptocurrency transactions into the rules. Crypto service providers and related trade groups generally opposed that provision, while some banks, money services businesses, and associations supported it. Opponents cited technological limitations, the lack of an international messaging standard for crypto transactions, and potential constraints on innovation.

Existing compliance obligations at centralized exchanges continue under applicable rules. Commenters noted that some potentially illicit transfers below $3,000 were already reported through Suspicious Activity Reports. Broader objections included claims that the proposal would violate the U.S. Constitution’s Fourth Amendment protections against unreasonable searches and seizures.

Agencies Cite Crypto Market Changes and Stablecoin Law

The agencies identified the proposal’s age and developments in the crypto industry as their two primary reasons for withdrawal. More than five years had passed since the agencies published the proposal in October 2020, and they considered further public feedback useful before adopting similar amendments. They said no final rule on those amendments would be issued without another opportunity for public comment.

Maturing markets and emerging legal frameworks also informed the decision, including the GENIUS Act’s payment stablecoin framework. Enacted July 18, 2025, the law established federal rules for companies issuing payment stablecoins. Officials said potential crypto-related amendments should reflect these developments.

Last month brought separate wallet and mixer proposal withdrawals involving self-hosted wallets and cryptocurrency mixing. Those proceedings addressed different proposed obligations from the international transfer threshold. The wallet proposal would have added recordkeeping for certain transactions above $3,000 and reporting for those above $10,000.

title: Strive buys 15,124 Bitcoin in October, closes in on top treasury holders
summary: Bitcoin treasury company Strive reported $509 million in third-quarter net income and purchased 15,124 BTC in October, bringing its total holdings to 43,124 BTC.
content:
Bitcoin treasury company Strive purchased 15,124 Bitcoin (BTC) in October, bringing its total purchases for the first 10 months of 2026 to 35,497 BTC, according to its third-quarter earnings report released Friday. The purchases brought the company closer to the top of the corporate Bitcoin treasury rankings.

Strive reported that it held 43,124 BTC as of Oct. 30, making it the fourth-largest publicly traded corporate Bitcoin holder, according to BitcoinTreasuries.NET data. It trails third-place Twenty One Capital by just 390 BTC and would need another 877 BTC to surpass second-place Metaplanet, which holds 44,000 BTC, assuming neither company increases its holdings.

Strive’s accumulation follows comments made by CEO Matt Cole in a September interview, in which he said the company could become the world’s second-largest publicly traded corporate Bitcoin holder by year-end, although he acknowledged that the outcome was not his base-case scenario.

Strive’s Bitcoin accumulation over the past month. Source: BitcoinTreasuries.NET

Strive also raised approximately $609 million in net proceeds through an October offering of its SATS perpetual preferred stock, which carries a 15% annual dividend rate. The company has not specified how much of the proceeds it will allocate to Bitcoin purchases.

Strive reported $509 million in third-quarter net income, driven largely by $533.7 million in unrealized Bitcoin gains.

Strive eyes banking and DeFi expansion

According to its earnings report, Strive is also evaluating opportunities in banking, brokerage, decentralized finance, reinsurance and tokenization as part of a broader strategy to leverage its balance sheet.

Jeff Walton, Strive’s chief risk officer, told Cointelegraph that the company is looking beyond cryptocurrency markets for ways to put its Bitcoin holdings to work.

“We believe that some of the bigger opportunities are crossing the aisle into traditional finance, operating as a structured finance company, and finding yield and distribution that is not correlated to Bitcoin or crypto,” Walton said.

Shares of Strive (ASST) fell 1.97% to $20.19 in early trading Friday, extending their decline over the past month to 32.15%, according to Yahoo Finance data at the time of writing.
