title: Coinhub Brand Enters Simulated Prop Trading Through Nevis Firm
summary:
Coinhub Funded has launched a simulated proprietary trading programme that combines evaluations and instant funding with up to nine short weekday trading tournaments. 
Coinhub Is Not the Prop-Firm Operator 
The launch announcement connects the new business with Coinhub’s network of more than 2,000 B...
content:
2026-11-06T20:18:00.000+02:00

Friday, 06/11/2026 | 18:18 GMT by Tanya Chepkova

  • A Nevis company has launched Coinhub-branded prop accounts that pay traders for simulated results.
  • Separate USDT tournaments run alongside the programme, but winning one does not qualify a trader for a funded account.

Coinhub Funded has launched a simulated proprietary trading programme that combines evaluations and instant funding with up to nine short weekday trading tournaments.

Coinhub Is Not the Prop-Firm Operator

The launch announcement connects the new business with Coinhub’s network of more than 2,000 Bitcoin ATMs across the United States. However, the network and the prop firm have different operators.

The ATM network is operated by Nevada-based LSGT Services LLC under the Coinhub trade name. Coinhub Funded’s client agreement instead names Block Entertainment Operating LLC, a company registered in Nevis.

According to the launch announcement, the prop firm uses the Coinhub name and logo under an intellectual property licensing agreement.

Funded Accounts Run on Simulated Trades

Under the prop firm’s terms, both evaluations and funded accounts operate in a demo environment. No trades reach the real market, and traders do not manage the operator’s capital.

The company describes payouts as performance-based commissions calculated from simulated results and says it does not operate as a broker, dealer or investment adviser.

Traders enter the funded programme by purchasing a one- or two-step evaluation and meeting its targets on a simulated account. They can skip that stage by buying an Instant Funding account, but the faster track has tighter risk limits and a lower ceiling: $25,000 in virtual capital, compared with $200,000 on the two-step programme.

Traders may hold several accounts, provided their combined starting allocation does not exceed $500,000. Both routes use the same simulated platform for crypto, forex, indices, metals and commodities.

Traders Receive Payouts in USDT

Payments depend on the results recorded there, not on the advertised account size. The standard commission is 80% of qualifying simulated profits.

Traders who pass an evaluation can raise their share to 90% by purchasing an add-on; Instant Funding keeps the 80% rate. Eligible traders can request payouts at 14-day intervals, in USDT or cash at cash-enabled Coinhub ATMs.

Each account also has a lifetime payout limit equal to its starting virtual balance and closes once that limit is reached.

Coinhub Funded also schedules up to nine short simulated tournaments on weekdays. Some have paid entry and USDT prizes, but winning a tournament does not qualify a trader for a funded account; that remains a separate programme accessed through an evaluation or Instant Funding.

title: Bitcoin price dips under $75K as crypto markets miss tech-stock rebound
summary: BTC price action stayed weak after US nonfarm payrolls data significantly beat forecasts, increasing bets of a December interest-rate hike.
content:
Bitcoin (BTC) set new multi-week lows after Friday’s Wall Street open as BTC price action diverged from stocks.

Key points:

  • Bitcoin fell to $74,762 after the start of Friday’s US trading session, its lowest level since Aug. 21.
  • Investors piled into tech stocks after Thursday’s sell-off, with the Nasdaq Composite Index gaining 1.8% in the first hour.
  • BTC price analysis warned that $69,000 could return if 50-week trend line support gave way.


Bitcoin extends losses after US jobs data beats forecasts

Data from TradingView showed BTC/USD dipping below $75,000 to levels last seen in mid-August. The total crypto market cap was down 0.5% on the day.

BTC/USD one-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView

US stock markets rebounded as traders took advantage of heavily discounted tech shares. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite Index traded up 0.6% and 1.2%, respectively, at the time of writing.

Nasdaq Composite Index one-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView

Certain tech stocks saw much sharper gains, with SanDisk and Micron Technologies both up 6.3%.

US nonfarm payrolls data released on Friday showed that the economy added 165,000 jobs in October, well above market expectations of 65,000. September’s 29,000 figure was also revised upward to 60,000.

“Employment increased in professional and business services, in health care, and in transportation and warehousing,” an official release from the US Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) reported, adding that the unemployment rate was now 4.1% versus a predicted 4.2%.

US civilian unemployment rate. Source: BLS

Stronger labor-market performance can create a headwind for crypto and risk assets as it suggests that the economy can manage any financial policy tightening, which in turn can reduce liquidity inflows to the market. 

On the back of the latest data, expectations of the Federal Reserve hiking interest rates by 25 basis points at its December meeting increased from 66.9% to 76.8%, per data from CME Group’s FedWatch Tool. 

Fed target-rate probability comparison for December FOMC meeting (screenshot). Source: CME Group

Related: Here’s what happened in crypto today


Analysis sees potential BTC price drop to $69,000

Bitcoin tested support around its 50-week simple moving average (SMA) at $77,533.

BTC/USD one-day chart with 50-week SMA. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView

In his latest market analysis, Keith Alan, cofounder of crypto trading platform Material Indicators, warned of the consequences of losing the trend line, which has acted as support since mid-September.

“As strong as this support level looks from both a technical and structural perspective, we can’t confirm its durability before the W close,” he wrote on X, referring to the weekly candle close. 

Alan saw a drop to as low as $69,000 for BTC/USD should the area around $75,500 fail to hold. A recovery, he said, depended on the pair producing a series of higher highs and higher lows on lower time frames.

title: Thailand SEC Files Criminal Complaint Against Bitget Ahead of Dec. 5 Access Block
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Thailand SEC Files Criminal Complaint Against Bitget Ahead of Dec. 5 Access Block
Thailand's SEC filed a criminal complaint against Bitget operator BG Limited for unlicensed Thai trading from 2022 to 2025.
This post Thailand SEC Files Criminal Complaint Against Bitget Ahead of Dec....
content:
Thailand’s Securities and Exchange Commission filed a criminal complaint Thursday against BG Limited, the operator of cryptocurrency exchange Bitget, alleging it ran an unlicensed digital-asset exchange for Thai users from 2022 to 2025, and notified the government to block the platform from Dec. 5.

The complaint, lodged with the Economic Crime Suppression Division, also names Mr. Kritsana Kritsananuwat as an alleged supporter who promoted Bitget through Facebook and YouTube channels, the SEC said in statement No. 241/2026.

From 2022 through 2025, the regulator found, Bitget offered a trading system in the ordinary course of business, charged fees, ran a Thai-language website that could show values in baht, and solicited Thai users on social channels including “Bitget Thailand” on X, “BGB Thai Holder” on Telegram and “bitgetthailand” on TikTok.

That conduct amounts to operating a digital-asset exchange under Section 3 of the Emergency Decree on Digital Asset Businesses B.E. 2561 (2018) without a license, a violation of Section 26 punishable under Section 66, the SEC said. The case now moves to an inquiry official, then prosecutors and the courts.

Separately, the SEC submitted Bitget’s website, other domains and its app to the Ministry of Digital Economy and Society under a 2025 royal decree that authorizes access blocks on unlicensed trading platforms. From Dec. 5, the public “will be unable to access the platform,” the statement said, and investors still holding assets there were told to consider acting before the cutoff.

A licensed path that now sits next to a criminal case

The enforcement push lands weeks after Bitget announced a planned acquisition of GMO-Z.com Cryptonomics (Thailand), a Bangkok digital-asset exchange and brokerage that already holds Thai licenses, through its interest in BTGT Management (Thailand) Ltd.

Under that deal, GMO Internet and its Thai holding company would transfer their entire stake in GMO-Z — about 49% and 50.94%, respectively — to BTGT or a designee at completion, a Sept. 24 GMO Internet filing showed. Bitget said completion remains subject to regulatory approval and, after a change-of-control nod, it intends to introduce its trading platform to Thai users under local rules.

“Thailand is an important part of Southeast Asia’s digital asset landscape, and this acquisition gives us a great opportunity to establish local operations,” Bitget CEO Gracy Chen said in the Oct. 20 release.

The timetable has already slipped. GMO Internet Group pushed the effective date of the share transfer from Oct. 31 to Nov. 30, citing careful work on Thai regulatory applications and closing procedures. That revised date sits five days before the planned Bitget access block.

CoinDesk reported that Bitget’s own terms of use, updated in October, already list Thailand among jurisdictions where its services are prohibited, and that the SEC has not said whether the criminal complaint will weigh on the GMO-Z change of control.

What the block does and does not settle

Thailand has used the same access-blocking tool before. In mid-2025 the SEC referred Bybit, OKX and three other unlicensed platforms for a June 28 cutoff, telling users to move assets first. The Bitget action follows that template — and adds a criminal complaint against the exchange operator and a named promoter.

Licensed venues still sit at the center of Bangkok’s policy mix. Thailand has approved a multi-year capital-gains tax break only for trades on SEC-regulated platforms, and has been expanding regulated crypto products in derivatives and capital markets. Unlicensed platforms get the opposite treatment: investor alerts, access blocks and, now for Bitget, a police referral.

What is not yet clear is whether a criminal case against BG Limited for the 2022–2025 period bars, slows or leaves untouched BTGT’s bid to take over a licensed local operator. The SEC statement does not mention GMO-Z. Bitget has not publicly answered the complaint in a statement posted with the acquisition release.

For Thai users still on Bitget, the practical clock is Dec. 5. For Bitget, the test is whether Nov. 30 closes a regulated door into Thailand — or whether the complaint filed Thursday makes that licensed path the next question the ECD and the SEC have to answer.

Micah Zimmerman

title: Former FBI Agent Pleads Guilty to Stealing $2.47 Million in Crypto From Investigations
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Former FBI Agent Pleads Guilty to Stealing $2.47 Million in Crypto From Investigations
Patrick Steven Yaroch, 37, of Ashburn, Virginia, pleaded guilty Thursday to wire fraud and money laundering after using wallet credentials from 35 FBI investigations to take about $2.47 million i...
content:
A former FBI agent pleaded guilty Thursday to stealing about $2.47 million in cryptocurrency with wallet credentials the bureau had collected in its own cases, the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of Virginia announced.

Patrick Steven Yaroch, 37, of Ashburn, Virginia, entered pleas to wire fraud and money laundering in federal court in Alexandria. U.S. District Judge Patricia Tolliver Giles accepted the plea. He faces up to 20 years in prison and is scheduled for sentencing on March 4, 2027.

Court papers put the illicit haul at $2,474,380.66. Prosecutors say Yaroch made roughly 100 fraudulent transfers using credentials tied to 35 separate FBI investigations, drawing on wallets controlled by investigation subjects, adversarial nation-state actors and at least one wallet the FBI itself had created for an operation.

The Justice Department Office of the Inspector General had flagged the case in August after Yaroch’s arrest on a criminal complaint. That earlier account described a smaller set of transfers — about 10 moves totaling roughly $1 million — and noted that Yaroch self-reported the activity to two department employees on July 29, 2026. The plea figures are larger.

From 2017 through early 2025, Yaroch worked in the FBI Boston Division on a squad focused on an adversarial nation-state. From February 2025 through July 31, 2026, he served in the FBI’s Counterintelligence and Espionage Division at headquarters, with access to systems that stored cryptocurrency credentials gathered in investigations.

How the FBI credentials turned into cash

Beginning no later than December 2024, Yaroch used that access to move coins out of those wallets and into ones he controlled. After the transfers, he swapped the stolen cryptocurrency into other digital assets and ran further transactions meant to obscure its source, nature and ownership.

Between Nov. 25, 2025, and Jan. 13, 2026, he moved about $93,082 into one of his accounts, then shuffled funds among other accounts to cover debts, including credit cards, car payments and loans, the office said.

FOX 5 DC, citing the same U.S. Attorney’s Office release, noted the Portugal planning that appears in the plea papers. Yaroch asked ChatGPT how to maximize investment returns and where to live in the European Union. After the chatbot suggested buying a vineyard in Portugal, he gave Portuguese lawyers a power of attorney on June 15, 2026, to register him with the Portuguese Tax and Customs Authority, obtain a tax identification number and collect the password to his finance portal. He arranged travel to Portugal for September 2026.

What the plea says the FBI lost

The agreed statement of facts goes beyond the dollar figure. Yaroch’s conduct compromised multiple FBI investigations into criminal groups and nation-state adversaries, the office said, and it compromised FBI sources and methods used in foreign intelligence collection and criminal cases. It also “deprived FBI employees of their ability to carry out their functions to protect public safety and national security.”

First Assistant U.S. Attorney Theophani K. Stamos and Daniel S. Wierzbicki, special agent in charge of the FBI Washington Field Office’s Counterintelligence Division, announced the plea. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Kathleen Robeson and Russell Carlberg are prosecuting, with help from the National Security Cyber Section of the Justice Department’s National Security Division and the DOJ inspector general’s Mid-Atlantic region. The case is 1:26-CR-208 in the Eastern District of Virginia.

The admission lands in a week when federal crypto-crime stories keep stacking up — from a failed bitcoin kidnapping plot that produced its own guilty plea last month to FBI tallies putting U.S. crypto fraud losses above $11 billion in 2025, a figure the White House has used to frame a wider crackdown.

What sentencing will do with the gap between Yaroch’s July self-report and the $2.47 million plea figure is still open. So is how many of the 35 FBI cases can be repaired after an insider treated the bureau’s own wallet credentials as a personal ATM. March 4, 2027, is when Judge Giles gets to answer the first question.

Micah Zimmerman

Friday, 06/11/2026 | 16:30 GMT by Tareq Sikder

  • The event combines industry networking, a gala dinner and awards recognising financial services firms.
  • Retail FX brokers including CFI, Eightcap, Libertex, HFM and TMGM are among companies represented at the event.

The Finance Magnates Awards 2026 Gala Dinner and Ceremony is taking place today in Limassol, Cyprus, bringing together representatives from across the financial services industry.

London's trading industry is coming home!

The programme began with welcome drinks and networking from 18:30 to 20:00 local time, followed by guests entering the main hall and taking their seats.

Companies represented among the guests include AIFO, Axcera, Base Markets, CFI, FYNXT, FotMarkets, FundingPips, CPattern, Fundora, Match-Trade, Eightcap, Libertex, Excinity Connect, Overchain, TradingPRO, Tapaas, FiveComply, Headway, HFM, WeTrade, Brisk Markets, FXBO, TradingView, Freedom, TMGM, IQ Broker, Octrado and iSAM Securities.

Finance Magnates Sets Stage for Awards Ceremony

The evening's formal programme includes opening remarks, a gala dinner and the awards ceremony, scheduled to take place between 22:00 and 22:30.

The ceremony will announce this year's award winners, recognising companies and individuals across the financial services sector.

The awards jury comprises Rotem Amar, Co-Founder at FXEmpire, who was absent from the event; Pere Monguió, Co-CEO at FXStreet; Nikolai Isayev, Chief Operating Officer and Editor-in-Chief at FinanceFeeds; Itai Levitan, Head of Strategy at investingLive; and Yam Yehoshua, Editor-in-Chief at Finance Magnates.

Finance Magnates CEO Outlines Group's Expansion Plans

Following a welcome drinks and networking session, Finance Magnates CEO Neophytos Papageorgiou officially opened the third annual awards ceremony, welcoming industry representatives and outlining the company's plans to expand its intelligence and education businesses.

He said Finance Magnates wanted to become “a more useful partner to the industry”, helping businesses make decisions through timely reporting, reliable data, practical insight and professional education.

Papageorgiou also highlighted the group's wider operations under Ultimate Group, which brings media, events and marketing services together.

Addressing the purpose of the awards, he said the ceremony offered an opportunity to recognise achievements and “reflect on what we value as an industry”, including better service, useful innovation, strong leadership and client trust.

He also noted that CEO nominations had been introduced for the first time this year to recognise individual leadership alongside company achievements.

title: Strive (ASST) Posts $474.8 Million Common Net Income as Bitcoin Yield Hits 63.2%
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Strive (ASST) Posts $474.8 Million Common Net Income as Bitcoin Yield Hits 63.2%
Strive posted $474.8M in Q3 net income to common holders, almost entirely a $533.7M unrealized bitcoin gain, and touted 103.7% year-to-date outperformance versus bitcoin.
This post Strive (ASST) Posts ...
content:
Strive reported $474.8 million of net income attributable to common stockholders for the third quarter ended Sept. 30, a print that arrived Friday alongside a company claim that Class A total return had outperformed bitcoin by 103.7% year to date through the same date.

GAAP net income was $509.0 million, or $5.24 a share on a fully diluted basis. Almost all of that came from a $533.7 million unrealized gain on digital assets marked to fair value. Operating revenue for the quarter was just $2.7 million, so the earnings line is a treasury mark, not a fee business.

In a post on X that led with the outperformance figure, Strive also highlighted a year-to-date bitcoin yield of 63.2% and a bitcoin dollar gain of $9.00 per assumed diluted share outstanding, both measured through Sept. 30. Chairman and CEO Matthew Cole tied those metrics to the stock’s relative showing against the asset.

“Strive has continued to successfully execute on its treasury management strategy, delivering a strong bitcoin yield year to date in 2026, which I believe is the primary driver of our common equity’s outperformance relative to Bitcoin so far this year,” Cole said in the earnings release.

Bitcoin yield, buys and the preferred stack

Bitcoin yield, as Strive defines it, is the percentage change in bitcoin per share over a period — not a cash yield. On that measure the company posted 18.5% in the third quarter alone and 19.3% from Oct. 1 through Oct. 30, after the SATS preferred debut.

Strive acquired 8,136 bitcoin in the third quarter at an average cost of about $78,885 and 20,373 bitcoin over the nine months ended Sept. 30. Another 15,124 coins followed between Oct. 1 and Oct. 30. Holdings stood at 28,000 bitcoin on Sept. 30 and 43,124 by Oct. 30, keeping Strive among the largest public corporate stacks after recent multi-thousand-coin buys and smaller weekly adds that still trailed Strategy.

Digital assets at fair value were $2.34 billion on the Sept. 30 balance sheet. Cash had risen to $490.4 million by Oct. 30, and Strive still held Strategy’s variable-rate STRC preferred with a fair value of about $50.1 million.

The capital stack that funded the buys is mostly perpetual preferreds. On Oct. 20 Strive closed a registered offering of 7 million shares of its 15% Series A perpetual preferred (SATS) for about $609 million in net proceeds. Preferred dividends of $34.2 million in the quarter are what turned the $509.0 million GAAP profit into the $474.8 million common figure.

Strip the story to nine-month GAAP and the picture flips. For the nine months ended Sept. 30, Strive posted a net loss attributable to common stockholders of $88.4 million. The third-quarter profit is real under fair-value accounting, but it is concentrated in one mark-to-market line.

What ASST stock has done over the past year

ASST itself has not moved in a straight line with the company’s bitcoin-yield scoreboard. Shares closed at $20.59 on Thursday, down about 10% on the day, and traded near $20.70 early Friday. That leaves the stock roughly 29% below its level a year earlier, when Yahoo Finance data put the close near $29, and about 33% under its Oct. 21 local high of $30.75.

The 52-week range on Yahoo Finance runs from $7.02 to $34.40. Year to date, the price path from the Jan. 2 close near $17.30 into the mid-$20s is a gain of roughly 20%, with a February low near the 52-week floor and a September push back toward $30. Through Sept. 30 — the cutoff on Strive’s outperformance claim — ASST had risen about 70% from that January close while bitcoin was down roughly 7% over the same window on Yahoo Finance data, a wide gap even before the company’s own total-return methodology.

The longer chart still carries the scar of 2025, when Asset Entities became the public shell for Strive’s bitcoin-treasury reverse merger and the share price spiked into triple digits on weekly closes before collapsing. Investors who held through that conversion saw a different ride than the tidy year-to-date relative-return figure Strive put at the top of Friday’s note.

Cole said the recent SATS issuance leaves Strive “never been in a better position to generate long-term returns in excess of Bitcoin for our common equity shareholders.” The test for ASST from here is whether another quarter of bitcoin yield and preferred-funded buys can reopen the gap to bitcoin after a year in which the stock still sits well below where it traded twelve months ago, even as the treasury has climbed past 30,000 then 40,000 bitcoin.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: Xlence is kicking things off in style! Partnering with Bundesliga Club 1. FSV Mainz 05.

The partnership marks a significant step in Xlence's international growth strategy, strengthening its brand presence and creating new opp...

Disclaimer

  • Xlence partners with Mainz 05 as Official Internationalization Partner.

Xlence has officially announced a strategic sponsorship agreement with German Bundesliga club 1. FSV Mainz 05, becoming its Official Internationalization Partner. The partnership marks a significant step in Xlence's international growth strategy, strengthening its brand presence and creating new opportunities to engage with even broader audiences.

The agreement brings together the online trading brand and an established European football club, combining Xlence's international ambitions with the global appeal of professional football. Through this collaboration, Xlence aims to expand its reach, strengthen brand awareness, and develop meaningful connections with audiences through a range of marketing and digital initiatives.

Strengthening Xlence's International Presence

The partnership with 1. FSV Mainz 05 represents an important development in Xlence's efforts to establish a stronger international presence and connect with audiences beyond traditional financial services channels.

As a recognised Bundesliga club, 1. FSV Mainz 05 provides a platform for reaching football audiences and exploring new opportunities for international brand awareness. The partnership creates a foundation for Xlence to develop its presence across markets while building an association with European professional football.

The collaboration also reflects Xlences's commitment to exploring new approaches to brand development. By bringing together the worlds of online trading and football, the partnership opens opportunities for marketing initiatives that support the brand's international growth objectives.

Upcoming Bundesliga Branding and Digital Activations

As part of the sponsorship, Xlence is preparing a series of promotional activities designed to bring the partnership to life.

One of the first initiatives being explored is the introduction of Xlence's virtual branding through LED advertising visuals during 1. FSV Mainz 05's upcoming Bundesliga fixture against FC Bayern.

The proposed matchday activation would mark an important first step in showcasing the partnership and introducing Xlence to football audiences through a prominent Bundesliga fixture. The branding arrangements remain subject to final confirmation.

Beyond matchday visibility, the partnership will include plans for website branding updates, digital activations and additional collaborative marketing initiatives. These activities aim to strengthen awareness of Xlence and create opportunities to engage audiences through multiple digital channels.

Further partnership initiatives and content collaborations are expected to be introduced as the agreement develops.

Building Connections Beyond Borders

The Xlence and 1. FSV Mainz 05 partnership brings together two organisations with a shared ambition to expand their international reach and connect with audiences across different markets.

For Xlence, the agreement represents more than a sponsorship opportunity. It establishes a foundation for ongoing collaboration, international brand development and engagement through one of the world's most widely followed sports.

As the partnership moves forward, Xlence looks to build on this collaboration through new digital experiences, coordinated marketing activities and initiatives that strengthen its relationship with wider audiences.

title: Binance, Deribit Kill SignalPlus API Keys After $82K Social Engineering Breach
summary:
Key Takeaways: Binance and Deribit removed all the API keys associated with SignalPlus. The losses haven’t exceeded $82,000, SignalPlus said, and its users will be reimbursed. The attack started with
The post Binance, Deribit Kill SignalPlus API Keys After $82K Social Engineering Breach appeared fir...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Binance and Deribit removed all the API keys associated with SignalPlus.
  • The losses haven’t exceeded $82,000, SignalPlus said, and its users will be reimbursed.
  • The attack started with a compromised Telegram account and a fake Microsoft Teams invite.

Binance and Deribit have disabled API keys connected to SignalPlus after the crypto derivatives infrastructure provider disclosed a cyberattack that compromised one of its engineers.

The exchanges claimed that there were no issues with their systems. Binance also stated that no funds of its users had been lost, and Deribit identified no signs that its systems or data were compromised.

  • Binance and Deribit Cut SignalPlus Access
  • Fake Teams Invite Compromised an Engineer
    • IP Whitelisting Becomes a Key Failure Point
    • Crypto Firms Face Another Social Engineering Warning

Binance and Deribit Cut SignalPlus Access

SignalPlus said the incident began early on Nov. 4 and affected a small number of accounts that did not use IP whitelisting.

TL;DR: In the early hours of Nov 4, SignalPlus was targeted in an attack that began with a compromised third-party Telegram account, affecting a small number of accounts without IP whitelisting.

We detected and contained the intrusion quickly. As a precaution, we immediately worked with our CEX partners to revoke all SignalPlus-linked API keys and temporarily paused our terminal services.

Total losses are under US$82k, and all affected users will be reimbursed in full.

We expect to bring services fully back online over the next few days. Updates and user instructions will be shared through our official channels.

— SignalPlus (@SignalPlus_Web3) November 5, 2026

The company reported this suspicious activity to its centralized exchange partners and requested them to suspend all of SignalPlus’s API keys. The system also shut down its trading terminal in the course of a comprehensive security audit.

Binance CEO Changpeng Zhao advised all connected SignalPlus users that they should also cancel their other API credentials. 

Yi He, Binance’s co-founder, independently urged third-party platforms connected to Binance to check security measures and keep an eye out for any unusual activity.

We also encourage all third-party platforms integrated with Binance to review their security controls, monitor for unusual activity and contact us immediately if they detect any concern💁🏻‍♀️
This is not a challenge for any single company……

— Yi He (@heyibinance) November 5, 2026

The solution has effectively blocked trading, monitoring and automated execution via SignalPlus during the credential revocation period.

Read More: Binance Reveals How Hackers Moved $6.34B After Breaching Its Wallet-Signing System

Fake Teams Invite Compromised an Engineer

SignalPlus has identified that the attack is from a Telegram account of a contact at one of its external technology providers.

The attacker pretended to be that contact, and sent a fake invitation to a SignalPlus engineer. After infecting the engineer’s computer, the intruder sat silent until he was able to exploit his employee’s access to the company’s internal network.

SignalPlus states it did detect it, block the activity and closed the vulnerabilities it identified.

IP Whitelisting Becomes a Key Failure Point

The company also admitted that access to the exchange API was not IP address whitelisting. If not, the stolen credentials can be used from attacker-controlled infrastructure based on the permissions set on the key.

SignalPlus also will adjust API-access, endpoint security, internal permissions and key-management access. The company says total losses due to the incident are less than $82,000 and affected users are being reimbursed in full.

Crypto Firms Face Another Social Engineering Warning

The leak comes on the heels of another $6.3 billion crypto heist at Binance on Oct. 29.

Binance later stated that the attack was made through hacked employee computers, which included an engineer who was targeted using a fake job interview. The FBI would credit the attack to the North Korean hacking group.

While they occurred separately, both demonstrate trends of attacking employees or trusted third party relationships, rather than just attacking exchange infrastructure.

SignalPlus states that services will be back on a phased basis once security reviews and patches have been implemented. Users can still manage positions and open orders directly through the exchanges while the SignalPlus terminal remains suspended.

title: Rule to Allow Crypto in 401(k)s Arrives at White House for Final Review
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Rule to Allow Crypto in 401(k)s Arrives at White House for Final Review
A final Labor Department rule that would create a fiduciary safe harbor for private equity, real estate and crypto in 401(k) menus arrived at OIRA on Thursday, putting public release within reach.
This post Rul...
content:
A final DOL rule that would ease alternative assets such as private equity, real estate and cryptocurrency into 401(k) retirement plans arrived at the White House on Thursday for review, Bloomberg Law reported, a procedural step that usually precedes public release.

The Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs logged the package on Nov. 5 under the title “Fiduciary Duties In Selecting Designated Investment Alternatives,” RIN 1210-AC38. The filing lists the DOL’s Employee Benefits Security Administration as the authoring office, marks the stage as a final rule, flags it as economically significant and notes that there is no legal deadline for completion.

The DOL unveiled the proposal on March 30. In that draft, plan fiduciaries who follow a documented process when adding private assets to a 401(k) menu would get a legal safe harbor under the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974.

The six factors named in the proposal are performance, fees, liquidity, valuation, performance benchmarks and complexity. Satisfying them does not force plans to offer crypto. It lowers the litigation risk for employers that decide they want to.

What the DOL safe harbor covers

President Donald Trump’s Aug. 7, 2025, executive order, “Democratizing Access to Alternative Assets for 401(k) Investors,” directed the Labor secretary to reexamine ERISA guidance and, where appropriate, propose rules with “appropriately calibrated safe harbors.” The order defined alternative assets to include private-market equity and debt, real estate, holdings in actively managed vehicles that invest in digital assets, commodities, infrastructure and lifetime-income strategies.

The March proposal implements that order. A DOL fact sheet said prudence under ERISA is process-based and that fiduciaries retain discretion to select any designated investment alternative if they follow the outlined review. Deputy Labor Secretary Keith Sonderling cast the approach as neutral: “The department’s days of picking winners and losers are over.”

That stance reverses a prior chill. In May 2025 the DOL rescinded its March 2022 compliance release that told fiduciaries to use “extreme care” before putting cryptocurrency on a 401(k) menu. The department said that phrase was not found in ERISA and restored a context-specific standard.

Later, it was reported that Sens. Bernie Sanders and Elizabeth Warren pressed the DOL to abandon the crypto-friendly path. House Republicans have separately pushed to codify Trump’s crypto order in statute.

Why OIRA review matters for bitcoin and crypto

OIRA review under Executive Order 12866 is the last interagency checkpoint before a final rule can be published in the Federal Register. Bloomberg Law said the arrival signals the package is nearing completion. The same office cleared the proposed version in late March before the DOL published it; that earlier pass took roughly two months after the January submission, per prior Bloomberg coverage of the roughly $12 trillion 401(k) market.

What is not yet public is the final text itself. Whether the six-factor safe harbor survived comment intact, how digital-asset vehicles are described, and what effective date the DOL chose will only be clear when OIRA returns the rule and the department posts it. Comment volume on the proposal was heavy; industry and labor groups have argued opposite sides of the prudence standard for months.

For bitcoin, the stakes sit in plan menus rather than spot ETF flows. Trump’s August order helped frame digital assets as a retirement-access issue for more than 90 million defined-contribution savers. A finalized DOL safe harbor would not put bitcoin and crypto on every lineup overnight. It would give plan committees a clearer map if they want exposure through an asset-allocation sleeve that holds digital assets.

The test now is how fast OIRA clears the economically significant package — and whether the published final rule still gives fiduciaries the process cover the March draft promised, or whether the comment fight rewrote the safe harbor before the White House stamps it.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: DraftKings Raises Predictions Investment to $650M–$700M as DKeX Gross Take Rate Reaches 11.1%
summary:
DraftKings is expanding a prediction market business from the client app to the exchange, even as the investment is set to absorb most of the Adjusted EBITDA expected from its established operations this year.
DraftKings has increased its expected 2026 Adjusted EBITDA investment in Predictions to be...
content:
2026-11-06T17:01:39.641+02:00

Friday, 06/11/2026 | 15:01 GMT by Tanya Chepkova

  • Predictions will absorb most of the Adjusted EBITDA DraftKings expects from its core business in 2026.
  • The company expects its first Predictions customer cohort to repay acquisition costs in about 20 months.

DraftKings is expanding a prediction market business from the client app to the exchange, even as the investment is set to absorb most of the Adjusted EBITDA expected from its established operations this year.

DraftKings has increased its expected 2026 Adjusted EBITDA investment in Predictions to between $650 million and $700 million, sharply reducing its group profit forecast despite continued profitability in its established sportsbook and iGaming business.

Overall third-quarter revenue rose 16% year over year to $1.33 billion. However, the quarterly Adjusted EBITDA loss widened to $316.9 million from $126.5 million.

The company now expects full-year Adjusted EBITDA of $175 million to $275 million, down from its previous forecast of $700 million to $900 million.

Its core business is still expected to produce between $875 million and $925 million, but most of that contribution is being absorbed by the expansion of prediction markets. Predictions will require another $175 million to $225 million of Adjusted EBITDA investment in the fourth quarter alone.

DraftKings also expects the unit’s 2026 net revenue to remain immaterial because promotions for new customers will offset most of the gross revenue generated. The company disclosed the revised guidance alongside its third-quarter results.

Owning DKeX Expands the Revenue Stack

To explain the larger investment, DraftKings provided its first detailed figures on how it earns revenue from trades on DKeX. During September and October, trades on DKeX generated an average gross take rate of approximately 11.1% across brokerage, exchange operations and market making.

DraftKings captured about two-thirds of that gross revenue, while external market makers received the remainder. Unlike a broker that only distributes contracts from another exchange, DraftKings controls the client interface, the DKeX exchange and its own market maker.

This allows it to earn revenue at several stages of a transaction, although the company is currently returning much of that income to customers through promotions.

DraftKings reported that more than 1.6 million customers had interacted with Predictions since the beginning of 2026. At October’s pace, customer trading volume would reach $10.1 billion on an annualised basis, almost three times July’s rate.

Total volume, which also includes market-maker activity, would annualise to $56.8 billion at October’s pace. That larger figure should not be treated as customer turnover when assessing retail adoption.

The company said its 2026 customer cohort was running at approximately $350 million in annualised Adjusted Gross Profit. It expects to recover the cost of acquiring those customers in about 20 months.

The run rate extrapolates recent performance; the projected payback has not yet been achieved. The operating metrics appear in DraftKings’ third-quarter business update.

DraftKings Models a Future without Sports Contracts

For 2027, DraftKings expects Predictions to generate between $650 million and $750 million in revenue while requiring another $250 million to $350 million of Adjusted EBITDA investment.

The company expects the unit to generate positive free cash flow in 2028 and to improve group Adjusted EBITDA that year. DraftKings separately modelled a less favourable outcome amid disputes over whether prediction markets can offer sports contracts without state gambling licences.

In a scenario where sports event contracts cease in July 2028, management estimates that customers acquired in 2026 would repay their acquisition costs before that date. The 2027 cohort would be more than halfway to repayment by July 2028 and could recover its costs within roughly four years even without sports contracts.

DraftKings says it will adjust its Predictions investment as the regulatory position develops, so its spending forecast is not fixed regardless of the outcome.

title: Binance Hackers Swap About $50 Million of Stolen XRP Mostly Into Bitcoin, Elliptic Says
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Binance Hackers Swap About $50 Million of Stolen XRP Mostly Into Bitcoin, Elliptic Says
About 42 million stolen XRP, worth roughly $50 million, has been swapped mostly into bitcoin via THORChain, Elliptic said, lifting converted bitcoin from the Binance theft to about 1,650 BTC.
Th...
content:
Hackers tied to the record Binance theft have begun converting a large slice of the stolen XRP into bitcoin, blockchain analytics firm Elliptic said in an update dated through Friday, with about 42 million XRP — roughly $50 million — already swapped, mostly through THORChain.

Converted bitcoin from other stolen assets nearly doubled overnight to about 1,650 BTC, worth some $124 million, Elliptic wrote. Most of that jump came from the XRP route. About 192 million XRP, roughly $226 million, remained unswapped in addresses linked to the Binance theft.

The XRP was part of the Oct. 29 drain that Binance later put at $6.34 billion. Between 20:05 and 20:09 UTC that day, five hot wallets sent 233.46 million XRP to an attacker address. The FBI has attributed the campaign to North Korea’s TraderTraitor group. Binance has reopened withdrawals in stages and said it has frozen or intercepted about $2.85 billion while covering customer losses from its own funds.

How the XRP started moving

The stolen XRP sat quiet at first. Early on Nov. 2, between 02:12 and 04:00 UTC, all about 233 million XRP moved into six new addresses, where it stayed until Nov. 5, Elliptic said. From the afternoon of Nov. 5, two of those six addresses began sending XRP on to dozens of new accounts that swapped it, mostly through THORChain into bitcoin.

A small amount of ether also went through THORChain into bitcoin that evening. The main bitcoin and ether holdings from the theft — the largest pools — have still not moved, Elliptic said. That pattern matches what the firm saw after the Bybit hack: turn freezable and mid-liquidity tokens into bitcoin first, then attempt cash-out later through OTC brokers.

The broader laundering trail is already vast. Since the Binance theft, Elliptic has counted more than 20,000 wallets on 16 blockchains, at least 36 services and at least 65,000 transactions — roughly one new wallet every 30 seconds and one transaction every 10 seconds. About $3.11 billion remains in addresses linked to the Binance theft, mostly as ether and bitcoin. A negligible amount has likely been cashed out so far.

Why XRP and bitcoin matter here

Issuers can freeze many stablecoins. They cannot freeze XRP the same way, and they cannot freeze bitcoin. After Tether and Circle locked down large stablecoin tranches on Oct. 29, the attacker prioritized assets that sit outside that kill switch. Swapping XRP into bitcoin continues that logic: bitcoin is harder to claw back once it is fragmented across fresh addresses.

All of the stolen SOL, about $87 million at Elliptic’s prices, has already been swapped, bridged or mixed, with much of it ending as bitcoin. Most early Tron laundering — about $220 million in TRX — has also run, a flow Bitcoin Magazine noted when covering the quiet shutdown of the T3 Financial Crime Unit before the hack. Only small parts of the main ether and NEAR piles have moved.

Some converted bitcoin has gone into Wasabi-style coinjoins — about 33 BTC, or $2.5 million, since Nov. 1 — and about $1.1 million in ether and SOL entered the Privacy Cash pool before that service paused deposits. Elliptic said the speed points to conventional automation, not an AI agent making live decisions: fixed timing, set amounts, blind retries and new tactics introduced hours apart.

U.S. bank supervisors have already checked in with lenders after the Binance breach. For bitcoin markets, the nearer question is how much more of the remaining ~192 million XRP — and eventually the parked ether — gets turned into BTC before anyone tries to cash out.

The test now is whether THORChain operators and other bridges keep blocking the published attacker addresses fast enough to slow the XRP-to-bitcoin pipe, or whether the rest of that pile follows the same overnight path the first $50 million already took.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

What Are the Best MetaTrader 5 Brokers in 2026?

The best MetaTrader 5 brokers in 2026 are seven international brokers that each lead on one MT5 need, so the right pick depends on how you plan to trade:

  • Admirals: Best for the most complete MT5 setup, with three MT5 accounts and a free plugin.
  • Pepperstone: Best for Razor pricing with 28 Smart Trader Tools.
  • IC (IC Markets): Best for raw pricing, with MT5 servers in the Equinix NY4 data center.
  • FP Markets: Best for a broad CFD lineup, with 800+ MT5 instruments across seven asset classes.
  • CMC Markets: Best for futures CFDs, within 1,100+ MT5 instruments.
  • Tickmill: Best for a $3 raw commission with hedging and automated trading allowed.
  • Exness: Best for currency choice, with 100+ pairs and a free VPS.

US residents should go to the US section, which covers FOREX.com and Trading.com.

1. Admirals

Admirals is a multi-asset broker whose group holds a CySEC license through Admirals Europe Ltd, and it runs three separate MT5 account types for different traders. The figures below come from its international site, which Admirals SC Ltd runs under the Financial Services Authority (FSA) of Seychelles.

Admirals offers the most complete MT5 setup on this list. Every Admirals MT5 account gets the MT Supreme Edition plugin for free.

Pros and Cons of Admirals

The pros and cons of Admirals come down to a wide choice of MT5 accounts on one side and an offshore entity for international clients on the other.

The pros of Admirals:

  • Three MT5 accounts: CFD, zero-spread and stock-investing accounts all run on MT5.
  • Free tools: MT Supreme Edition adds a mini terminal, a trading simulator and a spread recorder.
  • Fill record: The company reports 99.68% of orders filled at the requested price or better.

The cons of Admirals:

  • Tier-3 license: International clients join Admirals SC Ltd, which holds a Seychelles FSA license (SD073). The group’s CySEC license covers only Admirals Europe Ltd.
  • Regional terms: The EU site lists different spreads and deposits, so check the site for your country.
  • StereoTrader condition: StereoTrader is a one-click trading panel with 35+ commands, OCO orders and dynamic trailing. Free access needs €4,000 of equity on a live account.

2. Pepperstone

Pepperstone was founded in Melbourne, and its group holds FCA and ASIC licenses. MT5 is one of its five platforms, next to MT4, cTrader, TradingView and its own platform. International clients sign up with Pepperstone Markets Ltd, which the Securities Commission of The Bahamas (SCB) licenses.

Its place on this list comes from the extras it adds to MT5, because Pepperstone clients get the 28-app Smart Trader Tools package, and the Razor account adds raw forex pricing.

The pros and cons of Pepperstone balance strong MT5 extras and global reach against an offshore entity for international clients and a high share of losing retail accounts.

The pros of Pepperstone:

  • 28 Smart Trader Tools: The package adds expert advisors and indicators to MT5.
  • Global reach: The company reports 900,000 clients in 160 countries around the world.
  • Support team: Pepperstone’s support team works 24 hours a day on weekdays and 18 hours at weekends.

The cons of Pepperstone:

  • Tier-2 license: International clients join the Bahamas company, not the FCA or ASIC ones.
  • Loss rate: Its risk warning says 80% of retail CFD accounts lose money.
  • Account-based tools: Some tools may depend on the account type.

3. IC (IC Markets)

Pros and Cons of IC

The pros and cons of IC weigh low raw pricing and open trading rules against an offshore license and leverage that IC can change at any time.

The pros of IC:

  • Lower commission tiers: Larger deposits cut commission to $1.50 or $1.00 per side.
  • Open trading rules: IC sets no minimum order distance and allows hedging.

The cons of IC:

  • Tier-3 license: International clients deal with Raw Trading Ltd, which holds a Seychelles FSA license (SD018).
  • Changing leverage: IC can change leverage at any time, which can raise your margin needs.
  • Restricted countries: IC does not serve the US, Canada, Iran or North Korea.

The pros and cons of Tickmill set flexible account rules and swap-free options against an offshore entity for international clients and a higher starting deposit.

The pros of Tickmill:

7. Exness

Pros and Cons of Exness

The pros and cons of Exness set a low entry cost and raw pricing against weaker regulation, extremely high leverage and a long list of countries it does not serve.

The cons of Exness:

The free VPS is what sets Exness apart, because each one comes with 2 CPU cores and 2 GB of RAM, against 1 CPU core on IC’s entry VPS tier. An expert advisor can therefore keep trading while your own computer is off.

Which MT5 Brokers Accept US Traders?

MT5 brokers that accept US traders must be registered with the CFTC and be members of the NFA, and on our research date the two confirmed options are FOREX.com and Trading.com. Here is how the two compare for MT5 traders:

None of the seven international brokers above appears here, because none of their international sites lists a CFTC registration. Four of them, IC, CMC Markets, Tickmill and Exness, also state that they do not serve US residents.

No US regulator ranks brokers, so there is no official #1 broker in the US. Of the two, FOREX.com covers more markets on MT5, because it adds futures to forex, while Trading.com lists forex only.

Is MT5 Forex Trading Legal in the USA?

Yes, MT5 is legal in the USA, because it is trading software, and US citizens can use MT5 as long as the forex broker behind the account is registered with US regulators.

US rules on forex trading also limit leverage for retail traders, who must post at least 2% margin on major currency pairs and 5% on other pairs, so a $100,000 major-pair position needs $2,000.

Offshore dealers are the main risk for US forex traders, because the CFTC reports more fraud complaints from customers of unregistered offshore dealers, some of which block withdrawals until the customer pays extra fees. The CFTC lists high leverage above US limits as a warning sign of fraud, and NFA BASIC, the NFA’s online database, shows a firm’s registration and disciplinary history.

FOREX.com

FOREX.com gives US MT5 traders a forex account with extra tools and access to futures through its parent, StoneX Group, and the MT5 account adds these extras:

  • Tools: Over 20 expert advisors and custom indicators from FX Blue come with the account, along with integrated Reuters news.
  • VPS: FOREX.com offers free VPS hosting to MT5 customers who qualify.
  • Demo account: The MT5 demo comes with $50,000 in virtual funds and expires after 90 days.
  • Futures on MT5: Futures and futures options run through StoneX Financial Inc. and need a StoneX futures account and an MT5 subscription.

Trading.com

Trading.com is a forex-only option for US MT5 traders, run by Trading.com Markets Inc. from its office in New York, and its US offer is narrow:

  • Products: Trading forex is all you can do there, because forex is the only instrument type it lists for US clients.
  • Platforms: Trading.com offers MT5 next to its own WebTrader and mobile app.

How We Chose These MT5 Brokers

We chose these MT5 brokers with a three-part gate that every broker had to pass, and then we ranked the brokers that passed by the quality of their published MT5 data:

  • MT5 for international clients: The broker’s official site confirms that MT5 is open to clients outside a single home market.
  • Regulation: The broker’s group holds at least one Tier-1 license (FCA, ASIC, CySEC or CIRO) or Tier-2 license (FSCA, SCB or BMA).
  • Published MT5 data: The official site publishes at least two of three items: symbols on MT5, MT5 costs and MT5 tools.

The ranking then weighs three criteria together: how complete each broker’s official MT5 data is, the tier of its regulators, and its MT5 costs and tools.

All figures come from each broker’s official website, and we did not open live or demo accounts to test them. Size was not a criterion either, so one of the largest MetaTrader brokers, XM, is missing even though it reports more than 20 million clients. XM and FxPro both failed the gate because their official MT5 pages publish too little MT5-specific data to check.

US readers get a separate rule, CFTC registration plus NFA membership, because no other broker may serve them.

What Is MetaTrader 5?

MetaTrader 5 is a multi-asset trading platform that MetaQuotes released in 2010 for trading forex, stocks and futures, with more than 80 built-in analytics tools, and brokers license it and connect it to their own servers and prices.

Any forex broker that licenses MT5 from MetaQuotes can offer it, so the answer to “Which brokers have MT5?” is a long list, and the broker you pick matters more than the software itself.

Is MT5 Free?

Yes, MT5 is free to download and use with a broker account, and what you actually pay for are the broker’s trading costs, such as spreads, commissions and swaps, the overnight interest charged or paid on positions held past the daily rollover. Optional extras can cost money too, because MetaQuotes rents virtual hosting inside the platform after a 24-hour free trial, and some robots and indicators in the MT5 Market are paid. Some brokers cover the VPS instead, as IC does once a client trades 15 lots of forex and metals in a month.

Can You Use MT5 Without a Broker?

No, you cannot trade live on MT5 without a broker, but you can download the platform and open a demo account with virtual money to practice. MT5 asks you to pick a trading server when you open any account, and a live account always needs a broker’s server.

MT5 Desktop, Web and Mobile

The MT5 trading platform comes in three versions, a desktop app for Windows and Mac, a web version for any browser, and mobile apps for iOS and Android:

VersionBest forLimitation

WebTrading from any browser on Windows, Mac or Linux without installing software30 indicators and 9 timeframes, against 38 and 21 on desktop

MT4 vs MT5: Which Trading Platform Should You Use?

MT5 is the better choice for most traders in the MT4 vs MT5 question, because MetaQuotes built it with 21 timeframes against 9 on MT4, more pending order types and exchange markets that MT4 does not cover:

MT5 suits new traders and anyone who wants stocks or futures next to forex, with more order types on one trading platform. MT4 still makes sense if you rely on MQL4 expert advisors or indicators you already own, and our guide to the best MT4 brokers covers that platform.

Switching from MT4 to MT5 takes some work, because MT5 uses a different programming environment, so MT4 expert advisors and indicators do not run on MT5 until someone rewrites them in MQL5.

Best MT5 Broker for Beginner Forex Traders

The best MT5 broker for beginners is Pepperstone, because it has a $0 minimum deposit, a $10 minimum funding amount and 28 Smart Trader Tools for MT5. Exness is the other low-cost pick among the best brokers here, with a $10 Standard account, but its unlimited leverage means a beginner should keep positions small. Traders at all experience levels can lower their risk with three checks before funding an MT5 account:

  • Start on a demo account: Practice placing orders and setting stop losses with virtual money before you add real funds.
  • Check the minimum deposit: Entry accounts in this list start at $0 at Pepperstone and IC and reach $100 at Tickmill, so match the account to an amount you can afford to lose.
  • Check your add-ons: Confirm that the tools you want, such as Smart Trader Tools or MT Supreme Edition, come with your account type.

Is MT5 Safe?

Yes, MT5 is safe as online trading software, because MetaQuotes builds it as a legitimate platform that every broker here licenses, but your money’s safety depends on the broker entity.

MetaTrader 5 is not a broker, so “Is MetaTrader 5 a good broker?” has no direct answer, and MetaQuotes states that it provides no investment or brokerage services. The forex broker running your MT5 server sets your prices, holds your money and handles your orders.

Protection changes with the entity, even under one brand. Admirals SC Ltd in Seychelles insures client money for up to $100,000 if the company becomes insolvent, but not against trading losses. CMC Markets Bermuda gives retail clients negative balance protection, so they cannot lose more than they deposit. Tickmill’s UK and EU clients have compensation schemes of up to £120,000 and €20,000, which its Seychelles entity does not list.

Three checks tell you whether an MT5 broker is trustworthy with your money:

  • Entity name: Read the account agreement to see which company will hold your money and whether it keeps client funds in segregated accounts, apart from its own money.
  • Regulator tier: Check whether that company’s regulator is Tier-1, such as the FCA, ASIC or CySEC, Tier-2 or offshore.
  • Register lookup: Search the license number on the regulator’s own register, or on NFA BASIC if you live in the US, which also shows a firm’s disciplinary history.

How to Choose an MT5 Forex Broker

How to choose an MT5 broker comes down to seven checks, starting with the entity you join and ending with whether the broker serves the country where you live:

  • Regulation: Check the regulator of the entity you join, not only the licenses of the wider group.
  • Symbols on MT5: Count the instruments offered on MT5, not the broker’s total across all platforms.
  • MT5 account types and costs: Compare spreads and commission per lot on the account you will actually use, because a competitive spread on one account can come with a commission on another.
  • Non-trading fees: Look for withdrawal, inactivity and currency conversion fees on the broker’s fee page, and check how long withdrawals take to process.
  • MT5 tools and VPS: Check which add-ons and VPS terms the broker offers on your account type.
  • Minimum deposit and demo: Confirm the minimum deposit, the payment methods you can use and that a demo account is available.
  • Availability in your country: Make sure the broker serves residents of your country and offers customer support in your language.

The three brokers that publish a named MT5 add-on package offer these tools:

BrokerAdd-on packageNumber of toolsWho gets it
PepperstoneSmart Trader Tools and MyTrader28Pepperstone clients; may depend on account type
AdmiralsMT Supreme Edition60+Every Admirals MT5 account
FOREX.comFX Blue package20+ EAs and indicatorsIncluded with a FOREX.com MT5 account

Symbols on MT5 deserve a close look, because a broker’s headline number can cover every platform it runs. CMC Markets’ international site lists 12,000 financial instruments across all its platforms, while its Canadian MT5 page lists 1,100+ trading instruments, so a trader who only uses MT5 should plan around the smaller MT5 number.

How to Open an MT5 Demo Account or Live Account and Connect It to Your Broker

Opening an MT5 account and connecting it to your broker takes seven steps, and the order is similar at every broker in this list:

Step 1: Choose the broker and entity, check which company will open your account.

Step 2: Register and verify, complete KYC, the identity check, with an ID and proof of address.

Step 3: Choose an MT5 account type, select MT5 and pick a raw-spread or spread-only account.

Step 4: Fund the account, deposit from the broker’s client area, not inside MT5.

Step 5:Download MT5, install it on desktop or mobile, or use the web version.

Step 6:Log in, enter your account number, password and the broker’s server name.

Step 7: Test on demo first, before your first live order, place a test trade on a demo account with the same broker.

title: Europe’s Largest Asset Manager Amundi Brings €22.8B STOXX Europe 600 Fund to Ethereum
summary:
Key Takeaways: Amundi began a tokenized STOXX Europe 600 fund share class on Ethereum. The number of assets in the underlying index fund is approximately €22.8 billion. Amundi’s new launch
The post Europe’s Largest Asset Manager Amundi Brings €22.8B STOXX Europe 600 Fund to Ethereum appeared first o...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Amundi began a tokenized STOXX Europe 600 fund share class on Ethereum.
  • The number of assets in the underlying index fund is approximately €22.8 billion.
  • Amundi’s new launch takes its tokenisation strategy one step further than money market products.

The continent’s biggest asset manager gets more into the public blockchain infrastructure. Amundi has issued a tokenized share class of its Core STOXX Europe 600 fund on Ethereum, bringing a major European equity strategy onchain.

Europe’s largest asset manager has brought a flagship European equity index fund onto @ethereum, extending its tokenization efforts beyond cash management.

@Amundi_FR, which manages €2.4 trillion, has launched a tokenized share class of Amundi Core STOXX Europe 600, issued on Ethereum and developed with @CACEIS.

The fund tracks the STOXX Europe 600, an index of 600 large, mid and small cap companies across Europe, and is used as a core building block for portfolio allocation.

Amundi’s first tokenized share class, a money market fund launched with CACEIS in November 2025, was also issued on Ethereum.

Ethereum is the home of onchain finance.

— Ethereum Institutional (@ethereuminsti) November 5, 2026

The transfer broadens Amundi’s in-house program into cash management to diversify market exposure in equity assets while maintaining the traditional Amundi business model.

  • Amundi Takes a €22.8B Equity Fund Onchain
  • Ethereum Expands From Cash Funds Into Equities
    • A New Test for Public Blockchain Finance
    • Traditional Fund Structure Stays in Place

Amundi Takes a €22.8B Equity Fund Onchain

The new share class is based on units of Amundi Core STOXX Europe 600, a flagship share class strategy which follows 600 large, mid and small-cap Shares of Europe.

Ledger Insights estimates the total value of the fund’s assets under management to be around €22.8 billion, which makes the tokenization of the equity-index one of the largest in Europe so far.

These Tokenized Units are issued on the public Ethereum chain and were created by CACEIS who provides the technology and infrastructure for tokenization of the fund shares. Amundi stated that the blockchain based class is still within the existing fund framework; its investors will be able to use the product in conventional ways.

That is key: Amundi isn’t replacing the fund with a crypto-native offering. Rather, it’s developing an onchain distributional and settlement platform into an existing investment opportunity.

Read More: Ethereum Hegotá Upgrade Puts 2 EIPs at Center of 62-Proposal Crypto Shakeup

Ethereum Expands From Cash Funds Into Equities

The launch complements Amundi’s inaugural tokenized money market fund share class that was launched with CACEIS and also has been issued on Ethereum since November 2025.

Amundi then went even further with digital-asset initiatives such as the launch of a tokenized cash-management product and blockchain-based product treasury projects, including those in cooperation with CACEIS and Ant International.

A New Test for Public Blockchain Finance

Entering a wide open European equity series represents a bigger challenge for tokenized finance.

Money market funds are among the most traditional asset classes for real-world asset tokenization due to the short duration of the assets suited to digital cash-management. The other exposure type is equity index funds, which means that you have a long-term investment in a hundred or more listed companies.

Tokenized fund shares could enable quicker settlement, increased access, greater transparency and greater automation, said Amundi. The asset manager also aims to gradually create further institutional client and platform solutions based on tokens.

Traditional Fund Structure Stays in Place

The underlying portfolio is not affected by its Ethereum version. The tokenized share class does not replace the fund itself, as blockchain is, for now, just the infrastructure for the issuance, sustaining and future digital distribution of the shares.

Amundi hasn’t provided details of the size of the new tokenised share class, or whether other products could be introduced in the near future.

Nevertheless, a new multibillion-euro STOXX Europe 600 strategy is being brought onto Ethereum, beyond stablecoins and Treasuries/money market funds.

Still, bringing a multibillion-euro STOXX Europe 600 strategy onto Ethereum gives the network another institutional tokenization use case beyond stablecoins, Treasuries and money market funds.

title: Bitcoin Price Holds Near $75,000 After Hot October Jobs Report
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Bitcoin Price Holds Near $75,000 After Hot October Jobs Report
Bitcoin price held near $75,800 Friday after U.S. employers added 165,000 jobs in October, far above the 59,000 forecast, as December Fed hike odds climbed toward 80%.
This post Bitcoin Price Holds Near $75,000 After Ho...
content:
U.S. employers added 165,000 jobs in October, nearly three times the 59,000 economists expected, the Labor Department said Friday, and the bitcoin price briefly pushed above $76,100 before settling near $75,500, Bitcoin Magazine Pro data shows.

The unemployment rate edged down to 4.1% from 4.2%, beating the Dow Jones forecast that called for it to hold. Average hourly earnings rose 0.4% on the month and 3.1% over the year, both ahead of estimates, CNBC reported.

Prior months were revised higher as well. August payrolls moved to 186,000, an upward revision of 53,000, and September rose to 60,000 after a 31,000 upgrade, leaving the two-month total 84,000 stronger than first reported.

The print lands on a market still digesting Thursday’s Nasdaq-led rout. The bitcoin price had held near $76,000 into that close, dipped toward $75,200 late in the session, then recovered into the mid-$75,000s overnight before the 8:30 a.m. ET release. Spot bitcoin changed hands around $75,800 after the data, with a market cap of about $1.52 trillion and roughly $48 billion in trading volume over the past day, Yahoo Finance data indicated.

Bitcoin price reaction

Bitcoin price’s first move was a quick spike above $76,100, then a slide toward $75,600 before it settled back near $75,800. The range on the day has run from about $75,240 to $76,280, leaving the market little changed from its pre-release level even as rate futures repriced.

That muted finish fits the pattern after big macro prints. Most of the damage to the bitcoin price this week came from equity risk-off, not from the labor market itself, and a hot payrolls number mainly reinforces the path the Fed was already pricing.

CME FedWatch odds put roughly a 79% chance of a 25-basis-point hike at the Dec. 9 meeting after the release, up from about 70% into the open. The next employment report is due Dec. 4, five days before that decision, and the signal points the same way the last Fed hold did: stronger hiring and firmer wages leave less room for another pause.

Tech rout aftermath and ETF outflows

Thursday’s session still sets the floor under the bitcoin price. The Nasdaq Composite fell about 5.5% and dropped into correction territory, more than 10% below its recent high, while the S&P 500 lost about 4.4% and the Dow shed roughly 1,800 points, or 3.4%, CNBC reported.

The Magnificent Seven erased more than $1 trillion in market value. Nvidia alone lost more than 9%, wiping out roughly $440 billion in capitalization, as investors priced in a slower AI data-center buildout after the Democratic midterm sweep.

Bitcoin has traded with that AI-heavy complex for most of the year, so a correction in the Nasdaq has pulled the bitcoin price lower even when on-chain flows looked steady. Miners that leased power and floor space to AI tenants are caught in both trades.

Fund flows followed the risk-off tape. U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs posted $430.2 million in net outflows on Thursday, led by about $200 million from Fidelity’s FBTC and roughly $105 million from BlackRock’s IBIT, bringing week-to-date redemptions through Thursday to about $870 million.

Leverage kept the bitcoin price soft into the overnight. More than $1 billion in crypto positions were liquidated over 24 hours, mostly long bets built during Wednesday’s short-squeeze bounce that lifted bitcoin near $80,000.

What comes next for bitcoin price

Professional and business services led October hiring with 70,000 jobs, health care added 42,000, and transportation and warehousing gained 25,000. Manufacturing rose 19,000. The breadth undercuts the recent pattern in which health care carried most of the gains.

Policy risk has not eased either. House Democrats are already drafting their own market structure bill ahead of taking the committees in January, a backdrop that has hung over crypto equities since the midterm results first hit the bitcoin price.

Traders are watching whether the bitcoin price can defend the mid-$75,000 zone that held on election night and several times since August. A clean break would leave September’s low back in sight after a week that erased most of the post-election squeeze, now with a hotter labor market and firmer hike odds stacked on top.

At the time of writing, the bitcoin price is near $75,500.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

Washington, D.C., November 6, 2026 — The Digital Sovereignty Alliance (DSA), a nonprofit organization dedicated to advancing clear and ethical public policy, research, and education related to emerging technologies, participated in the Strobe Summit, where DSA Managing Director Adrian Wall moderated a fireside chat with former Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) Chair Christiopher  Giancarlo on the evolving regulatory landscape for digital assets and the future of financial markets.

Titled “Crypto at a Crossroads: Regulation, Institutional Adoption, and the Future of Financial Markets,” the discussion examined the path forward for U.S. digital asset policy amid legislative uncertainty and growing institutional interest in blockchain-based financial infrastructure. Drawing on his experience leading the CFTC and founding the Digital Dollar Project, Giancarlo emphasized an approach to regulation that combines clear exchange rules under existing CFTC authority with congressional action to address remaining gaps. The conversation also explored the implications of the GENIUS Act, including Giancarlo’s concerns about financial privacy and his view that dollar-backed stablecoins could become a 24/7 global payment rail, raising fundamental questions about how the dollar moves on-chain and who provides that infrastructure.

Wall and Giancarlo also examined the regulatory challenges surrounding prediction markets, perpetual futures, and decentralized finance (DeFi). Topics included the CFTC’s role in overseeing event contracts, bringing offshore derivatives activity into regulated U.S. markets, the potential for 24/7 trading, and establishing accountability for decentralized platforms without traditional intermediaries. The discussion highlighted the need for regulatory frameworks that address market integrity, cybersecurity, customer asset protection, and the operational realities of increasingly interconnected financial markets.

“Regulatory clarity requires more than new legislation. It requires rules that reflect how digital asset markets actually operate,” said Adrian Wall, moderator of the discussion. “The CFTC has existing authority to address important market structure questions, while Congress has a critical role in resolving regulatory gaps. Getting that balance right will determine whether the U.S. can bring more digital asset activity onshore, accelerate institutional adoption, and protect market participants without compromising innovation or financial privacy.”

DSA’s participation reflects its commitment to advancing informed policy dialogue and practical regulatory approaches that support responsible innovation, market integrity, and the integration of digital assets into the broader financial system.

About the Digital Sovereignty Alliance

The Digital Sovereignty Alliance (DSA) is a nonprofit social welfare organization committed to advocating for public policies that support ethical innovation in decentralized technologies, blockchain, cryptocurrency, Web3, and artificial intelligence. DSA conducts research, organizes educational events, and promotes policies that prioritize public welfare and digital sovereignty.
